papers.abstract: Self-attention plays a key role in long-sequence modeling, but its quadratic time complexity fundamentally limits the scaling of Large Language Models. Recently, Multi-State Linear Attention (MSLA) mechanisms have been proposed to make sequence modeling more efficient by splitting the context into segments and compressing each in its own memory state. MSLA aggregates the information extracted from each memory state using only the mean alignment between a query and each segment's keys, ignoring how the alignment is distributed within the segment. In order to model the relevance of a segment to a query more comprehensively and incorporate the variance of the alignment in the aggregation, we propose MERLIN (MomEnt Routing for multi-state LINear attention), a method that tracks the first and second moments of each segment's keys. Using the moments of keys, a query can recover both the mean and the variance of its alignment with each segment to perform a more content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts. Experiments on multi-state variants of Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and Mamba-2-780M show that MERLIN consistently outperforms existing aggregation methods on various long-context tasks. In particular, MERLIN outperforms baselines on RULER needle-in-a-haystack and long-context QA (+8.3% for Gated DeltaNet-1.3B and +7.0% for Mamba-2-780M) and diverse subtasks in LongBench (+13.5% and +12.0%). It even outperforms baselines that consume 4x more memory. MERLIN provides a simple and general routing mechanism for improving long-context capabilities of MSLA models.
authors: Hee Seung Hwang, Sanghyuk Chun, Xindi Wu, Olga Russakovsky, Zhiwei Deng
bullets: MSLA reduces the cost of long-sequence modeling by compressing context segments into separate memory states, but standard routing uses only mean query–key alignment.
MERLIN tracks each segment’s first and second key moments to estimate both mean and variance of query alignment.
This enables more comprehensive, content-aware aggregation of per-state readouts.
On RULER, long-context QA, and LongBench, MERLIN consistently outperforms existing routing methods, including baselines using 4× more memory.
Reported gains include up to 8.3% on RULER/QA and 13.5% on LongBench for the evaluated models.

figures.caption: Figure 1: (a) A multi-state linear attention (MSLA) model aggregates segment-level outputs via a weighted sum. Prior methods compute the weights λt,i from position or from the mean of each segment’s keys. MERLIN instead reads both the first and second moments of the keys. (b) On retrieval-augmented generation samples in HELMET (Yen et al., 2025), we measure the aggregation weight each method places on the ground truth (GT) segment at the query token. Position-based aggregation largely misses the GT and mean-based aggregation recovers more, while MERLIN places the most weight on it.

The final output is a weighted sum of segment-level outputs, where the weights are derived from a gated mix of the alignment mean and variance (step 3).

papers.abstract: Attention over tens of thousands of visual tokens dominates the inference of video diffusion transformers (DiTs). Existing methods reduce this cost through sparsity, low precision, or both, but use a single precision for all kept tiles. We observe that the output error introduced by approximation varies widely across tiles. Many tiles can be skipped with little error, others must be computed but gain little beyond low precision, and a few retain substantial error even at low precision. We present Triage, a training-free attention method that assigns each tile one of three approximation tiers: skipping it by replacing it with its block means, skimming it in NVFP4, or refining it with NVFP4 residual correction. A lightweight router predicts each tile's error under each tier from block statistics and moves a tile to a more accurate tier only when the predicted error reduction justifies the extra compute, with a single price setting this trade-off. A fused kernel executes all three tiers in a single pass on the FP4 tensor cores of RTX Blackwell GPUs. Across Wan2.2, HunyuanVideo, and LTX-2.5, Triage accelerates end-to-end generation by up to 2.32x over dense FlashAttention, and in each of five settings it runs faster than every baseline while reaching 0.3-3.0 dB higher PSNR than the highest-PSNR baseline.
authors: Yeonjae Kim, Omin Kwon, Seong Hoon Seo, Jae W. Lee
bullets: Targets the high inference cost of attention over tens of thousands of video tokens.
Assigns each tile to skip, NVFP4 skim, or NVFP4 residual refinement.
A lightweight router uses block statistics and one price parameter to balance error against compute.
A fused kernel executes all tiers in one pass on RTX Blackwell FP4 tensor cores.
Across three video diffusion models and five settings, it achieves up to 2.32× end-to-end speedup and 0.3–3.0 dB higher PSNR than the strongest baseline.

papers.abstract: Multi-modal video fusion aims to generate temporally coherent videos with salient targets and rich structural details by integrating complementary information from heterogeneous sensors. However, existing video fusion methods commonly rely on optical flow estimation and feature warping for inter-frame alignment and cross-frame information aggregation to maintain temporal consistency, thereby introducing considerable computational overhead and making the fusion performance vulnerable to flow estimation errors. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an efficient multi-modal video fusion network with dynamic region-guided temporal interaction. Specifically, the proposed spatio-temporal interaction module leverages the Test-Time Training paradigm to model temporal dependencies with linear complexity. Building on this design, the module restricts temporal modeling to key dynamic regions in the video sequence, as static background regions provide limited temporal cues. By excluding low-variation tokens from unnecessary temporal interaction, this selective strategy contributes to improved fusion quality and temporal consistency. In addition, leveraging the strong ability of pretrained MAE features to capture global structural dependencies, we introduce a feature-level temporal consistency constraint to suppress local flickering by aligning the inter-frame variation directions of the fused and source videos. We further propose a new MAE-based temporal metric that quantifies directional distance between their temporal variations within dynamic regions. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with existing state-of-the-art methods, our method achieves superior fusion quality and temporal consistency on multiple benchmark datasets, while exhibiting high computational efficiency under edge-device deployment settings.
authors: Jingxue Huang, Xiaosong Li, Yi Lin
bullets: Addresses the computational cost and error sensitivity of optical-flow-based frame alignment.
Uses test-time training for linear-complexity spatio-temporal interaction.
Focuses temporal modeling on dynamic regions while skipping low-variation background tokens.
Applies a pretrained-MAE-based consistency constraint to reduce local flickering.
Reports superior fusion quality and temporal consistency with high efficiency on edge-device settings across multiple benchmarks.

papers.abstract: Deep learning facilitates rapid single shot three dimensional (3D) reconstruction using fringe projection profilometry (FPP), but recovering accurate surface height from a single high frequency fringe image remains challenging because both long-range spatial consistency and fine geometric details must be preserved. Convolutional networks are limited in modeling long range dependencies, whereas window-based Transformers establish global interactions only progressively with increasing depth. To address these limitations, a hybrid Mamba Transformer network is proposed for fringe to height regression. The network adopts a Swin based U shaped architecture and introduces visual state space modeling at the intermediate resolution encoder stage. An axial and dilated vision state space (ADVSS) block is further developed to enhance prescan feature encoding through local, dilated, and axial depthwise convolutions while retaining four directional selective scanning. This design combines linear complexity long range modeling with direction aware preservation of local fringe structures. Experiments on a publicly available FPP dataset show that the proposed method outperforms hNet, SwinConvUNet, UHRNet, and HiDNet in mean absolute error(MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), absolute relative error, and structural similarity index measure (SSIM). Using only one deformed fringe image, the proposed method achieves an RMSE of 0.548 mm and an SSIM of 0.9985, reducing RMSE by 65.2% and 59.6% relative to UHRNet and HiDNet, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining selective state space modeling with hierarchical window based attention for accurate single-shot FPP reconstruction.
bullets: Addresses the difficulty of preserving both global spatial consistency and fine geometric details in single-shot fringe projection profilometry.
Uses a Swin-based U-shaped encoder–decoder with visual state space modeling at an intermediate resolution.
Introduces an axial and dilated vision state space block with local, dilated, and axial convolutions plus four-directional selective scanning.
On a public FPP dataset, outperforms hNet, SwinConvUNet, UHRNet, and HiDNet across MAE, RMSE, absolute relative error, and SSIM.
Achieves 0.548 mm RMSE and 0.9985 SSIM from a single deformed fringe image; evaluation is limited to the reported public dataset and metrics.

papers.abstract: Automated classification of gastrointestinal (GI) findings in endoscopic images could support early diagnosis, but architectures are often chosen on accuracy alone. We present a controlled, reproducible benchmark of ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 for eight-class GI classification on the public Kvasir dataset (4,000 images), using a stratified split (400 test images) and stratified group 5-fold cross-validation over all images. In cross-validation, ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 reached 92.12% and 91.70% accuracy, and a two one-sided tests (TOST) procedure showed equivalence within a +/-3 percentage-point margin (difference +0.43 points, 90% CI -0.33 to +1.18; p < 0.001). The architectures differed mainly in cost: ResNet50 had 3.6 times fewer parameters and 4.3 times fewer operations, 2.5-fold lower single-image CPU latency (69 vs. 177 ms) and 3.8-fold higher GPU throughput. Cross-validated calibration was similar (expected calibration error 0.021 vs. 0.023). An edge-oriented transformer, MobileViT-S, was most accurate on the test split (95.5%) but lost 9.4 points when an acquisition artefact present in some classes (the ScopeGuide inset) was occluded, whereas ResNet50 was not significantly affected. On 500 unseen polyp images with expert masks, both models' Grad-CAM maps focused on the lesion (3.6 times chance). On a de-duplicated external subset of GastroVision (1,998 images), accuracy fell to 78-80% for all three models and differences between them remained small. Accuracy differences between architectures were thus small relative to the effects of shortcut learning and domain shift, whereas efficiency differences were large. An efficient CNN is a defensible default for resource-constrained screening, but no model is deployment-ready without local validation.
bullets: On Kvasir’s eight-class task, ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 were statistically equivalent within a 3-point accuracy margin.
ResNet50 used fewer parameters and operations, with lower CPU latency and higher GPU throughput than ViT-B/16.
MobileViT-S achieved the highest test-split accuracy but was vulnerable to the ScopeGuide artefact, indicating shortcut learning.
Both ResNet50 and ViT-B/16 showed similar calibration and lesion-focused Grad-CAM explanations.
Accuracy dropped substantially on the external GastroVision subset, highlighting domain-shift risks and the need for local validation.

papers.abstract: High-resolution remote sensing (RS) imagery provides fine spatial detail over large areas, making it essential for fine-grained scene understanding. Referring Remote Sensing Image Segmentation (RRSIS) aims to segment regions described by natural language, yet many existing methods rely on sequential alignment--fusion pipelines with limited joint modeling of cross-scale visual hierarchies and linguistic dependencies. Moreover, dense attention mechanisms struggle with the sparsity and wide spatial dispersion of RS targets, while current datasets offer limited structured evaluation of multi-target references, multi-hop relational reasoning, and multi-granularity descriptions, limiting both model development and evaluation. To address these challenges, we propose a Cross-Scale Sparse Attention Model (CSSAM), which aligns multiscale visual features with complex referring expressions through two key modules. The Cross-scale Modality-aligned Fusion Module (CMFM) performs unified cross-scale cross-modal fusion, while the Dynamic Multimodal Sparse Hybrid Attention (DMSHA) selectively attends to informative visual--textual tokens, reducing dense visual interactions. Furthermore, we introduce M$^{3}$RRSIS-D, a RRSIS dataset explicitly designed around three core reasoning dimensions: multi-target (M$^{1}$), reference-dependent multi-hop (M$^{2}$), and multi-granularity (M$^{3}$) expressions. Extensive experiments on M$^{3}$RRSIS-D and two public RRSIS benchmarks demonstrate that CSSAM achieves competitive performance across accuracy, fine-grained reasoning, and high-IoU localization metrics, validating its effectiveness for complex semantic reasoning in realistic RS scenarios. Code, dataset, and model weights will be released upon acceptance.
authors: Yuxi Li, Lu Si, Xia Liao, Yidong Shen, Zheng Wei, Jun Zhang, Xin Yuan
bullets: Targets the difficulty of segmenting spatially sparse, widely dispersed regions described by complex natural-language references.
Uses CMFM for unified cross-scale cross-modal fusion and DMSHA to selectively attend to informative visual–textual tokens.
Introduces M³RRSIS-D, covering multi-target, reference-dependent multi-hop, and multi-granularity expressions.
Experiments on the new dataset and two public benchmarks report competitive accuracy, fine-grained reasoning, and high-IoU localization.
Code, data, and model weights are planned for release upon acceptance.

papers.abstract: We present HyScale, a long-context training system for learned sparse attention. Learned sparse attention is a promising architecture for million-token contexts, widely adopted in production since DeepSeek-V3.2. Selection, however, grows into the training bottleneck. For each query, it scores every previous token whereas sparse attention reads only $k$; worse, current systems materialize a full score table and repeat selection during recomputation. Our key insight is that the output of selection is not an activation, but rather a set of indices. Building on it, HyScale introduces HyTopK and selection replay. HyTopK finds each query's exact top-$k$ on the fly without a score table, while selection replay reuses forward-pass selection in recomputation. Together with holistic system optimizations tackling end-to-end training challenges, HyScale speeds up GLM-5.1 training on 1M-token sequences by 2.07$\times$ over Megatron-LM on 512 H20 GPUs. It also speeds up the CSA layers of DeepSeek-V4-Flash and the QSA layers of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next by 2.01$\times$ and 1.57$\times$ at 1M tokens on 32 H800 GPUs.
authors: Yangshen Deng, Xinjing Huang, Yulong Wang, Yunzhuo Liu, Jun Hu, Shuyong Tan, Chun-Chih Tseng, Mingji Han, Ray Ying, Key Zhang, Luo Mai
bullets: Learned sparse attention makes selection a training bottleneck because each query scores all prior tokens, despite reading only top-k tokens.
HyTopK computes exact top-k indices on the fly without materializing a full score table.
Selection replay reuses forward-pass selection during recomputation, reducing redundant work.
Combined with end-to-end system optimizations, HyScale achieves reported speedups of 2.07×, 2.01×, and 1.57× on 1M-token training workloads.
The evaluation covers GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash CSA layers, and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next QSA layers on H20 and H800 GPUs.

papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) process increasingly long sequences, attention becomes a major computational bottleneck. Sparse attention mostly targets inference, yet many methods still train densely or cannot support sparse training, and their added complexity makes sparsity hard to turn into wall-clock speedups, leaving dense attention widely used in practice. This paper introduces LazyFlash, a forward-dense, backward-sparse attention method built on the observation that attention training is dominated by the backward pass. LazyFlash keeps the forward pass exactly dense, so the trained model remains a standard dense model that existing systems such as vLLM can serve without any change. For the backward pass, LazyFlash proposes a gradient-aware block sparsification design that ranks query blocks by their attention-output gradient norms and skips those contributing negligibly to parameter updates, turning the dense backward into a block-sparse one. A gradient-mass budget adapts the amount of skipped computation to each head and training step, while importance sampling preserves the dense gradient in expectation. These designs are implemented inside the tiled FlashAttention backward kernel, where skipped blocks are never loaded or computed, translating gradient sparsity into real wall-clock acceleration. Experiments on long-context text and speech LLMs show that LazyFlash maintains downstream performance while achieving up to 5.7x attention-backward speedup over FlashAttention and 1.7x end-to-end training speedup.
authors: Keqi Deng, Ruchao Fan, Jinyu Li
bullets: Addresses the training-time bottleneck of dense attention, which limits practical speedups from sparse methods.
Uses gradient-aware block sparsification to rank query blocks by attention-output gradient norms and skip negligible updates.
Adapts sparsity with a per-head, per-step gradient-mass budget while importance sampling preserves dense gradients in expectation.
Integrates skipping into the tiled FlashAttention backward kernel, avoiding loads and computation for skipped blocks.
Maintains downstream performance while delivering up to 5.7× attention-backward and 1.7× end-to-end training speedups.
papers.selection_reason: Backward-sparse attention accelerates long-context LLM fine-tuning, directly fitting efficient attention and long-context methods.
papers.title: LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning
papers.tldr: LazyFlash accelerates long-context fine-tuning by keeping attention dense in the forward pass while skipping low-impact blocks during the backward pass.

papers.abstract: Sequence compression is a fundamental operation and a critical information bottleneck in efficient language and multimodal models, and yet prevailing approaches based on pooling or learned projections remain underperforming. We revisit sequence compression through the lens of test-time regression: input tokens define a regression problem whose fitted coefficients form the compressed representation. Importantly, the regression problem is learned end-to-end via backpropagation, while its coefficients are computed efficiently in closed form during the forward pass. This leads to TTR-Compressor, a general alternative to conventional pooling and projection-based compression. We evaluate TTR-Compressor as the compressor for block-wise sparse attention and the visual token merger for multimodal large language models. On block-wise sparse attention, TTR-Compressor improves RULER performance over attention-based compressors by a large margin. For visual token merging, it consistently outperforms the standard MLP merger and matches its performance with 55.6% fewer visual tokens. These results establish test-time regression as an effective primitive for sequence compression in efficient language and multimodal models.
bullets: Addresses the information bottleneck and limited performance of pooling- and projection-based sequence compression.
Computes regression coefficients in closed form during inference while learning the regression setup end-to-end with backpropagation.
Evaluated for block-wise sparse attention and visual token merging in multimodal large language models.
Achieves a large RULER improvement over attention-based compressors and matches an MLP merger using 55.6% fewer visual tokens.
Demonstrates test-time regression as a general compression primitive for efficient language and multimodal models.
papers.selection_reason: Test-time-regression sequence compression for sparse attention and visual token merging is an efficiency contribution.
papers.title: Rethinking Sequence Compression with Test-time Regression
papers.tldr: TTR-Compressor uses differentiable test-time regression to turn input-token relationships into compact representations, improving sequence compression for language and multimodal models.

papers.abstract: Generating 360-degree panoramas requires both local perspective fidelity and global spherical continuity. Existing representations face a trade-off: equirectangular projection (ERP) enables seamless panorama modeling but suffers from severe distortion and a domain gap to pre-trained image generators, whereas cubemaps preserve perspective geometry but often produce inconsistent faces and visible seams. We present Squaring-the-Sphere, a panoramic image generation framework built on a novel representation CubeAtlas, which unfolds all cubemap faces into a single compact canvas. By arranging orientation-aligned, rotated polar regions alongside the equatorial faces, this representation preserves the perspective geometry of cubemaps while organizing the cross-face relationships required for seamless panorama assembly. It further enables a pretrained diffusion transformer to model the complete panorama jointly in a single pass, without altering the backbone architecture or positional encoding. While CubeAtlas has a token count comparable to ERP, its structured layout makes many dense attention interactions unnecessary. We therefore introduce a layout-aware sparse attention mask that preserves the interactions required for panorama continuity while removing geometrically irrelevant token pairs. As a result, CubeAtlas achieves better quality than ERP modeling with lower attention computation. Furthermore, we introduce a training-free super-resolution technique and a fusion scheme that enhance fine details in distortion-free perspective space before achieving the final ERP panorama. Experiments on various benchmarks demonstrate that our method improves geometric fidelity, cross-view consistency, and high-resolution visual quality over previous methods.
authors: Xuhui Zuo, Chenjie Cao, Tengfei Wang, Junta Wu, Yisu Zhang, Chunchao Guo
bullets: Addresses the trade-off between ERP’s distortion and cubemaps’ cross-face seams.
Unfolds rotated cubemap regions into one compact, orientation-aligned canvas for joint panorama modeling.
Uses layout-aware sparse attention to preserve continuity while reducing unnecessary attention computation.
Adds training-free super-resolution and fusion in perspective space to improve fine details.
Experiments report better geometric fidelity, cross-view consistency, and high-resolution quality than prior methods.
papers.selection_reason: Layout-aware sparse attention for diffusion transformers reduces attention computation; transferable efficiency technique.
papers.title: Squaring-the-Sphere: Distortion-Free and Seamless Panorama Generation via CubeAtlas
papers.tldr: CubeAtlas enables distortion-free, seamless 360° panorama generation by jointly modeling cubemap faces with efficient sparse attention and perspective-space refinement.

papers.abstract: Point cloud transformers aim to capture detailed local geometry and relationships across a scene at a manageable computational cost. Two common approaches are window attention and global attention. They differ in how they enable scene-wide interaction, which refers to information exchange among tokens across a scene. Window attention reduces computational cost by restricting self-attention to groups of tokens called windows; in serialized designs, each window contains a fixed number of consecutive tokens from a spatially ordered sequence. Because each block only directly connects tokens within the same window, information exchange across windows relies on changes in window membership across blocks and hierarchical pooling. Global attention, in contrast, directly connects all tokens within a scene, but computing attention over all token pairs can be costly when the number of tokens is large. To balance computational cost and scene-wide interaction, we introduce MixPT, a point transformer that uses a mix of window and global attention blocks in an interleaved schedule, while retaining a single fixed serialization pattern for its window blocks. For scenes with a large number of tokens, MixPT applies global attention to spatially pooled tokens and returns residual updates to the original-resolution stream. Across indoor and outdoor benchmarks, MixPT achieves competitive accuracy with lower latency than representative window and global attention baselines. We further demonstrate the feasibility of scaling the attention stage in depth by repeating the interleaved pattern of window and global attention blocks.
authors: Minkyun Seo, Hyungtae Lim, Jaesik Park
bullets: Window attention lowers cost but limits direct communication across windows; global attention enables scene-wide interaction but is expensive for large token sets.
MixPT interleaves window and global attention blocks while keeping one fixed serialization pattern for window processing.
For large scenes, global attention operates on spatially pooled tokens and sends residual updates back to the original-resolution stream.
Experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks show competitive accuracy with lower latency than representative window- and global-attention baselines.
The interleaved attention pattern can be repeated to scale the attention stage in depth.
papers.selection_reason: Point transformer with interleaved window and global attention, contributing to efficient attention and 3D point cloud processing.
papers.title: MixPT: Point Transformer with Interleaved Window and Global Attention
papers.tldr: MixPT balances local detail, global scene interaction, and efficiency by interleaving window and pooled-token global attention in a point transformer.

papers.abstract: Sparse attention reads only a small subset of the key-value cache, and how to treat the unread tail remains a key challenge. Discarding the tail biases the output, and sampling it as previous approaches do fails at reads of 5% and below, where the tail likely holds heavy hitters the selector missed. Our key observation is that the simplest possible proxy, one token that folds the entire tail into its count-aware mean, already yields lower output error than a sample at every read behind a practical selector. We further show in closed form that at low reads sampling nearly doubles the weight error of discarding while a single proxy stays below it. Building on these findings, we explore approximating the dense attention distribution with a few proxies that target the tail. We propose OpenAttention, a pipeline of clustering, ErrorGate and top-k selection followed by a count-aware mean proxy. To implement clustering and selection both efficiently and effectively, we design training-free Query-Geometry Clustering (QGC) and a Query-Geometry Selector (QGS), which compress the keys while respecting the query directions. Additionally, unlike prior methods that rank clusters by centroid alone, ErrorGate allocates the exact read by the estimated weight error of each cluster. On RULER-32K HARD with Llama-3.1-8B, OpenAttention retains 99% of dense accuracy at a 1% read. It also achieves state-of-the-art accuracy across models, context lengths and datasets. Our customized attention kernel, OpenAttention.flash, runs the decode attention stage 10$\times$ faster than dense attention at a 1% read.
authors: Hyunwoo Yu, Jongbeom Lee, Hyunbin Kim, Sungjun Park, Jaemin Choi, Jincheol Yang, Seunghun Moon, Bongjoon Hyun, Kyomin Sohn, Kyeongbo Kong, Suk-Ju Kang
bullets: Sparse attention can be biased when unread tail tokens are discarded, while sampling performs poorly at very low read rates.
A single count-aware mean proxy for the entire tail reduces output and weight error more effectively than sampling.
The pipeline combines Query-Geometry Clustering, Query-Geometry Selection, ErrorGate, top-k selection, and tail proxies.
On RULER-32K HARD with Llama-3.1-8B, it retains 99% of dense accuracy at a 1% read.
OpenAttention.flash reports 10× faster decode attention than dense attention at a 1% read.
papers.selection_reason: Sparse attention with tail proxies and query-geometry clustering directly targets efficient KV-cache reading and attention acceleration.
papers.title: OpenAttention: One Percent Is Enough with Tail Proxies
papers.tldr: OpenAttention uses query-aware clustering, error-guided selection, and a count-aware tail proxy to preserve 99% of dense-attention accuracy while reading only 1% of the key-value cache.

papers.abstract: Kernelized attention provides a useful perspective for understanding self-attention as a similarity-based aggregation mechanism, but existing approaches often rely on fixed or stationary kernels, limiting their ability to adapt the similarity structure to complex token interactions. In this paper, we propose flow-based spectral kernel attention (FSKA), a framework for learning expressive nonstationary attention kernels. FSKA formulates kernelized attention through spectral density learning and parameterizes the resulting bivariate spectral density with normalizing flows. This design enables flexible and regularizable kernel learning while remaining compatible with scalable linear-attention computation. We further show that expressive kernel learning enables a simplified attention design with removed query--key projections and fixed orthogonal value projections, resulting in a more parameter-efficient architecture. Controlled experiments on classification, ablation, and scalability profiling show that FSKA achieves competitive or improved performance over existing attention mechanisms, while reducing projection-related trainable parameters by approximately $40\%$--$47\%$ compared with most baselines and maintaining favorable linear-attention memory scaling. Code Available: https://github.com/ziyang18/FSKA.
authors: Zi Yang, Ying Li, Alejandro Lancho, Dar\'{i}o C. Larese, Pablo M. Olmos, Michael Minyi Zhang
bullets: Addresses the limited adaptability of fixed or stationary kernels in kernelized self-attention.
Learns a bivariate spectral density using normalizing flows for expressive, regularizable kernel modeling.
Removes query–key projections and fixes orthogonal value projections to simplify the attention architecture.
Reports competitive or improved results in classification, ablation, and scalability experiments.
Reduces projection-related trainable parameters by approximately 40%–47% versus most baselines while retaining favorable linear-attention memory scaling.
papers.selection_reason: Learnable nonstationary attention kernels with linear-attention memory scaling fit efficient-attention research.
papers.title: Flow-based Spectral Kernel Learning for Nonstationary Attention
papers.tldr: FSKA learns flexible nonstationary attention kernels with normalizing flows, enabling parameter-efficient linear attention with competitive performance.

papers.abstract: Global warming and climate change are major catalysts for plant diseases, significantly affecting food production worldwide. Addressing this issue requires continuous monitoring and early detection of plant diseases. While recent advancements in deep learning offer potential solutions, most models demand high processing power and struggle to perform efficiently on low-end electronic hardware. Furthermore, many existing works focus on specific crop diseases, limiting their broader applicability. This paper presents a lightweight Group Equivariance Attention Network (GANet) designed for the prediction and monitoring of 38 types of plant diseases. GANet introduces a novel Group Attention block and Group-Wise Feature Fusion block, making it both sparse and efficient. With only 0.001M parameters, the model achieves an impressive 99.99% accuracy on the PlantVillage dataset. Additionally, GANet is optimized for deployment on edge devices such as the Raspberry Pi 4b and Jetson Nano, where it reaches 5 FPS and 11 FPS, respectively, demonstrating its potential for real-time plant disease monitoring on low-power devices.
authors: Anubhab Tripathi, Bibek Das, Asfak Ali, Sheli Shinha Chaudhuri
bullets: Targets efficient, broad plant-disease monitoring where conventional deep-learning models are too resource-intensive.
Introduces Group Attention and Group-Wise Feature Fusion blocks to produce a sparse, lightweight architecture.
Contains 0.001M parameters and achieves 99.99% accuracy on the PlantVillage dataset.
Runs at 5 FPS on Raspberry Pi 4b and 11 FPS on Jetson Nano, supporting edge deployment.
Scope is demonstrated on PlantVillage and the specified embedded platforms.
papers.selection_reason: Lightweight group attention network for edge deployment; directly relevant to efficient attention and low-resource inference.
papers.title: GANet: A Lightweight Group Attention Network for Plant Disease Identification on Embedded Systems
papers.tldr: GANet is a highly compact attention-based network for recognizing 38 plant diseases on low-power edge devices in near-real-time.

papers.abstract: Increasing the attention context length significantly improves streaming video generation quality, while incurring prohibitive memory and computational costs as the context grows. Existing methods attempt to capture this contextual information through attention selection or compression, but remain limited by bounded representations and lack explicit attention-level supervision to retain historical contributions to current queries. To address this, we introduce Attn-Forcing, a novel framework that preserves full-context attention contributions for streaming video generation under bounded memory and computation. We achieve this by introducing attention proxies that continuously approximate the attention responses induced by the historical context. Specifically, we implement the proxies as learnable visual latents and employ a Proxy Update Module to incorporate visual context from historical latents. Moreover, we propose an Attention Matching Loss to explicitly constrain the attention behavior of the learned proxies using full-context attention supervision. Extensive qualitative and quantitative experiments demonstrate that Attn-Forcing consistently improves streaming video generation quality and achieves state-of-the-art performance over existing baseline methods.
authors: Junyao Gao, Sibo Liu, Jiaxing Li, Yanan Sun, Hanxin Zhu, Weidong Zhang, Jun Zhang, Cairong Zhao
bullets: Longer attention contexts improve quality but create prohibitive memory and computational costs.
The method uses learnable visual latents as attention proxies for historical context.
A Proxy Update Module continuously incorporates context from historical latents.
An Attention Matching Loss provides explicit supervision from full-context attention behavior.
Experiments report consistent quality improvements and state-of-the-art performance over existing baselines.
papers.selection_reason: Learns full-context attention proxies for streaming video generation under bounded memory/compute; relevant to efficient attention and video generation.
papers.title: Attn-Forcing: Learning Full-Context Attention Proxies for Streaming Video Generation
papers.tldr: Attn-Forcing enables higher-quality streaming video generation by approximating full-history attention with learned visual proxies under bounded memory and computation.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward visual geometry models, exemplified by VGGT, have demonstrated strong multi-view reconstruction capabilities through dense global attention. However, the resulting all-to-all cross-view computation scales quadratically with the number of input views, making long-sequence inference particularly expensive due to substantial frame-level redundancy among highly overlapping observations. We uncover a topology-first, geometry-later evolution in VGGT camera tokens: shallow-layer tokens reliably capture local view neighborhoods, whereas deeper-layer tokens progressively encode globally organized inter-view geometry. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BlazeVGGT, a training-free framework for structure-aware frame-level key--value sparsification. At each global-attention block, BlazeVGGT constructs a view-level similarity kernel from camera-token relations and employs greedy determinantal point process inference to select a compact set of mutually complementary views. The selected views constitute the key--value context, while all input frames are retained as queries. This asymmetric attention design preserves dense per-frame predictions while eliminating redundant cross-view computation, allowing our method to be directly integrated into pretrained VGGT as a plug-and-play module without parameter updates. Its advantages become increasingly pronounced with sequence length: at 2,000 frames, BlazeVGGT achieves approximately 13$\times$ faster inference than VGGT while reducing the Chamfer Distance from 0.41 to 0.32. Extensive experiments demonstrate a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off in point-cloud reconstruction and camera-pose estimation, compatibility with existing VGGT accelerators such as FastVGGT and LiteVGGT, and transferability to VGGT-based models including StreamVGGT and PAGE-4D. Codes are publicly available at https://github.com/MagiciannnY/BlazeVGGT.git.
authors: Shujun Yao, Junhui Lin, Congying Han, Tiande Guo, Ziwen Liu, Bonan Li
bullets: VGGT’s all-to-all attention becomes costly for long, highly overlapping image sequences.
The method uses camera-token similarities to identify local-to-global view structure across network layers.
Greedy determinantal point process selection chooses complementary frames as sparse key–value context, while retaining all frames as queries.
At 2,000 frames, inference is approximately 13× faster and Chamfer Distance decreases from 0.41 to 0.32.
The plug-and-play approach transfers to VGGT variants and supports point-cloud reconstruction and camera-pose estimation.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces BlazeVGGT, a training-free framework for sparsifying camera tokens in multi-view geometry models, fitting 3D Vision and Efficient AI.
papers.title: BlazeVGGT: 13x Faster VGGT at 2,000 Frames via Camera Token without Training
papers.tldr: BlazeVGGT makes VGGT about 13× faster on 2,000-frame sequences by sparsifying redundant cross-view attention without retraining, while improving reported reconstruction accuracy.

papers.abstract: Full 3D attention is costly in video Diffusion Transformers. Block-sparse attention reduces this cost by computing only selected attention blocks. However, existing methods either overlook the potential to optimize sparsity allocation or rely on heuristic rules or local metrics to guide it. In this work, we observe that sparsifying attention in different layers and at different denoising steps affects final-video fidelity to substantially different degrees. Yet the identities of the most sensitive layer-step pairs remain nearly unchanged across inputs. Building on these findings, we propose Allocating Layer-step Latency by Output Tests (ALLOT), a training-free sparsity allocation method. Treating each layer-step pair as a cell, ALLOT estimates each cell's contribution to final-video error through (i) cell probing and (ii) trajectory calibration, then jointly optimizes cell densities under a measured-latency budget. It preserves existing selection strategies and kernels, replacing only the allocation component. At equal or shorter wall-clock time, ALLOT outperforms every compared allocation strategy with XAttention, with an 11.8 dB PSNR gain on HunyuanVideo. Extensive experiments across four additional published pipelines on Wan2.1, Wan2.2, and HunyuanVideo show that ALLOT outperforms or ties the default in all nine settings.
authors: Tianze Xia, Xiaoling Zhou, Ruya Lan, Yiqiao Liao, Chengru Song, Shiming Xiang
bullets: Full 3D attention is expensive, and different layer–step pairs have unequal effects on final-video fidelity.
ALLOT estimates each pair’s error contribution using cell probing and trajectory calibration.
It jointly optimizes sparsity densities under a measured-latency budget while retaining existing block-selection strategies and kernels.

Across five video diffusion pipelines and nine settings, ALLOT outperforms or matches the default allocation; with XAttention, it achieves an 11.8 dB PSNR gain on HunyuanVideo at equal or lower runtime.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes ALLOT, a training-free method to optimize block-sparse attention allocation in Video Diffusion Transformers, directly addressing efficiency and video generation.
papers.title: Sparsity Should Be ALLOTted by Output: Training-Free Allocation of Block-Sparse Attention for Video Diffusion Transformers
papers.tldr: ALLOT is a training-free method that allocates block-sparse attention across layer–denoising-step pairs to improve video diffusion quality under a latency budget.

papers.abstract: Synthesizing high-fidelity 7T MRI from routinely acquired 3T scans offers a practical pathway to enhanced neuroimaging without the prohibitive cost of ultra-high-field scanners. While existing deep learning approaches have achieved promising results, state-of-the-art methods typically rely on either large-scale architectures exceeding 45 million parameters or computationally intensive ensemble strategies, limiting their practicality in resource-constrained clinical environments. In this work, we propose a compact multi-domain attention framework, termed DGCM-SSFA, that achieves competitive synthesis quality with only 11M parameters. The proposed architecture integrates two complementary modules into a U-Net Transformer backbone. First, a Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulated Feature Modulator (DGCM) is embedded at multiple hierarchical levels to enhance local edge and texture details through Sobel-guided spatial attention and depthwise frequency-aware channel attention with cross-branch gating. Second, a Sparse Strip Frequency Attention (SSFA) module at the bottleneck captures global spatial context via strip-pooled attention with near-linear complexity, while simultaneously performing FFT-based spectral modulation in the frequency domain. These two modules operate synergistically with the backbone's native channel attention, forming a triple-granularity feature refinement pipeline. Extensive experiments on the UNC and BNU 3T-to-7T MRI datasets across T1w and T2w modalities demonstrate that DGCM-SSFA achieves strong structural fidelity, attaining an SSIM of 0.8431 on BNU T2w---approaching the best benchmark value of 0.8624---and 0.8100 on BNU T1w, while using substantially fewer parameters than Transformer-based alternatives such as ResViT (123.4M) and FS-RWKV (45.4M).
authors: Zhichun Fan, Zhiqiang Chen, Lanling Liu, Lingjun Liu, Zhonghua Xie
bullets: Addresses the high cost of 7T MRI and the impractical computational demands of existing synthesis models.
Combines dual-granularity cross-modulated feature refinement with sparse strip spatial and frequency-domain attention in a U-Net Transformer.
Uses Sobel-guided spatial attention, frequency-aware channel gating, strip-pooled global context, and FFT-based spectral modulation.
Evaluated on UNC and BNU datasets for T1w and T2w MRI; it achieves SSIM values of 0.8431 on BNU T2w and 0.8100 on BNU T1w.
Offers substantially fewer parameters than cited Transformer alternatives, including ResViT (123.4M) and FS-RWKV (45.4M).
papers.selection_reason: Compact MRI synthesis architecture with sparse strip frequency attention near-linear complexity provides transferable efficient attention ideas.
papers.title: DGCM-SSFA: Dual-Granularity Cross-Modulation and Sparse Strip Frequency Attention for Efficient 3T-to-7T MRI Synthesis
papers.tldr: DGCM-SSFA enables efficient 3T-to-7T MRI synthesis with competitive structural fidelity using only 11M parameters.

papers.abstract: Blind all-in-one image restoration must adapt a shared model to heterogeneous and sometimes mixed degradations without a task label at test time. We introduce WaFIR, a decoder module that decomposes features into Haar subbands, summarizes each subband with a compact Fourier descriptor, and routes it to prompt-conditioned spectral modulation experts. Unlike image-level frequency conditioning, WaFIR makes routing decisions at the subband level, enabling frequency-specific processing while retaining the task context learned by the backbone. Under a unified training and evaluation protocol for denoising, deraining, and dehazing, WaFIR improves average PSNR over the three tasks by 0.48 dB over the PromptIR baseline and by 0.38 dB over the recent Up-Restorer. Matched-capacity and routing controls show that the gain is not explained by additional parameters alone. On unseen noise intensities, descriptor-based routing is more robust than a discrete label-conditioned alternative and remains on par under compound degradations, while routing analyses show stable subband-dependent expert use across degradation types. These results support subband frequency structure as an interpretable complement to prompt-based conditioning for blind image restoration. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/WaFIR/README.md
authors: Trong Nhan Nguyen, Vu Hoang Minh Doan, Thanh Dat Le, Truong Tien Vo, Thi Thu Ha Vu, Tan Hung Vo, Jaeyeop Choi, Junghwan Oh, Truong-Son Hy
bullets: Targets denoising, deraining, and dehazing without degradation labels at test time.
Decomposes features into Haar subbands and makes frequency-specific, subband-level routing decisions.
Combines subband Fourier descriptors with prompt-conditioned spectral modulation experts.
Improves average PSNR by 0.48 dB over PromptIR and 0.38 dB over Up-Restorer under a unified protocol.
Routing remains robust to unseen noise intensities and compound degradations, with stable subband-dependent expert usage.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces subband-adaptive routing with Fourier descriptors and sparse spectral modulation, offering a transferable efficient attention design.
papers.title: WaFIR: Wavelet-Fourier Mixture-of-Experts with Subband-Adaptive Routing for Blind All-in-One Image Restoration
papers.tldr: WaFIR improves blind all-in-one image restoration by routing Haar subbands to prompt-conditioned spectral experts using compact Fourier descriptors.

papers.abstract: Transformers are deployed as a special model class. Neural processing units (NPU) add dedicated operators for attention and normalization, and quantization relies on Transformer-specific algorithms. We show the computation does not force this. Every Transformer block, with attention, LayerNorm and a GELU MLP, compiles exactly into a generic deep neural network built from fixed affine maps, routing and the square, sigmoid and inverse square root, plus GELU or its sigmoid approximation. Without activation-activation products, every transform-wise compilation adds at least $N^2$ scalar nonlinear evaluations per head for dense scores. Keeping that one operation type removes this cost; its elementwise form, present on every surveyed NPU, suffices with the sigmoid and inverse square root. For top-$k$ attention with exchangeable tail scores, we prove that exact or conditional-mean tail mass gives an unbiased, minimum-mean-square-error estimate of the attention distribution, while tail drop is conditionally biased. When queries or agents cluster, centroids choose the keys first, reducing the number of computed scores from $N^2$ to $Nk$ per head. On DeiT-Tiny, MambaIRv2-Light and Pythia-70M the compiled models match their references with all keys, standard post-training quantization applies, and the exact tail-mass estimate beats tail dropping with half as many keys on DeiT-Tiny and, for $k\le8$, on Pythia-70M.
authors: Sergey Salishev, Zeev Volkovich, Oleg Granichin
bullets: Every Transformer block—including attention, LayerNorm, and GELU MLPs—can be represented using fixed affine maps, routing, square, sigmoid, inverse square root, and GELU-related operations.
Removing activation-activation products incurs at least N² additional scalar nonlinear evaluations per head for dense attention scores; retaining elementwise products avoids this cost.
For top-k attention with exchangeable tail scores, exact or conditional-mean tail-mass estimates are unbiased and minimum-MSE, unlike conditionally biased tail dropping.
Clustering queries or agents selects keys through centroids, reducing per-head score computation from N² to Nk.
Compiled models match reference models with all keys, support standard post-training quantization, and show improved approximation from tail-mass estimation on the reported models.
papers.selection_reason: Reduces attention score computation via clustering and tail-mass estimation; fits efficient attention.
papers.title: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation-Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering
papers.tldr: Transformers can be compiled exactly into generic neural-network operations, while clustered top-k attention reduces computation and principled tail-mass estimation improves approximation over tail dropping.

papers.abstract: Large Language Model inference over long contexts is increasingly bottlenecked by the cost of attending to a growing Key-Value (KV) cache. Sparse attention reduces this cost by accessing only a fraction of the cache, but existing methods face a trade-off between deterministic retrieval, which captures high-scoring tokens but discards residual attention mass, and sampling, which improves coverage at the cost of higher variance. Hybrid methods combine top-$k$ retrieval with uniform sampling, yet still exhibit a substantial gap from dense attention at aggressive sparsity. We introduce \emph{Stratified Sparse Attention (SSA)}, a unified framework combining deterministic retrieval with score-guided sampling. SSA deterministically attends to high-scoring tokens while sampling the residual using proxy attention scores and correcting for their inclusion probabilities, thereby recovering attention mass beyond the retrieval set. SSA encompasses top-$k$, top-$p$, and hybrid top-$k$+sampling as special cases. Across RULER, LongBench, LOFT, and AIME, and five models ranging from 3B to 27B parameters, SSA consistently improves over the baselines at matched sparsity. On RULER-HARD with Ministral-3-8B, SSA improves accuracy over the strongest practical baseline from 81.8\% to 84.2\% at 32K and from 63.8\% to 69.3\% at 128K under $50\times$ attention sparsity, recovering 94\% and 85\% of dense-attention performance, respectively. With optimized CUDA kernels, SSA achieves up to $2.96\times$ decode speedup over FlashInfer at 1M context, demonstrating that its accuracy gains translate into practical long-context inference acceleration. We open-source our code at https://github.com/skylight-org/SSA-Paper-Code.
authors: Sahil Joshi, Prithvi Dixit, Aryan Katiyar, Agniva Chowdhury, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Anshumali Shrivastava, Aditya Desai, Kumar Krishna Agrawal
bullets: Targets KV-cache attention costs for long-context LLM inference, where sparse methods lose attention mass or suffer sampling variance.
Combines deterministic selection of high-scoring tokens with score-guided sampling of residual tokens and inclusion-probability correction.
Generalizes top-k, top-p, and hybrid top-k-plus-sampling methods.
Improves matched-sparsity performance across four benchmarks and five models, including stronger RULER-HARD accuracy at 50× sparsity.
With optimized CUDA kernels, reaches up to 2.96× decode speedup over FlashInfer at 1M-token context.
papers.selection_reason: Stratified sparse attention improves long-context efficiency by combining retrieval and sampling, directly relevant to efficient attention and KV cache.
papers.title: Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity
papers.tldr: Stratified Sparse Attention narrows the accuracy gap between sparse and dense attention at extreme sparsity while enabling faster long-context inference.

papers.abstract: Head-dimension compression can reduce the memory required by the key-value (KV) cache, but existing methods often reconstruct full-dimensional representations during inference, adding significant decoding FLOPs overhead. We formalize the design considerations for converting pretrained attention into a natively reduced-dimensional form that reduces both KV-cache storage and attention computation using a calibration set. Specifically, we consider reductions that (1) apply a shared projection to queries and keys so that they remain in a common reduced feature space, (2) derive this projection jointly from query and key activations to better preserve their interaction, and (3) are compatible with the pretrained RoPE transformation. To obtain a reconstruction-free realization of this reduction, we restrict it to coordinate selection and theoretically show that RoPE compatibility then holds if and only if complete rotary pairs are retained. Building on this characterization, we introduce RACE, a post-training method that selects rotary pairs using their joint query-key activation energy. We theoretically show that this criterion minimizes a separable, calibration-dependent upper bound on post-RoPE query-key product approximation error. The resulting reductions are folded into the model weights and require neither runtime reconstruction nor specialized kernels. Across three model families and different compression levels, RACE outperforms structured pruning and remains competitive with reconstruction-based methods on language-modeling, zero-shot, and long-context tasks. At 50% KV-cache retention and 256K context, RACE reduces total inference FLOPs by 47.8%, yielding 1.79x higher throughput, 43.2% lower time-to-first-token (TTFT), and 28.1% lower allocated GPU memory in comparison to an uncompressed model.
authors: Irene Tenison, Abdulrahman Alabdulkareem, Daniel Karl I. Weidele, Nima Dehmamy, Dan Gutfreund
bullets: Targets head-dimension reduction while avoiding the decoding FLOPs overhead of reconstructing full-dimensional keys and values.
Uses a shared query-key projection derived from calibration activations and retains complete rotary pairs to preserve RoPE compatibility.
Selects rotary pairs by joint query-key activation energy, minimizing a separable upper bound on post-RoPE query-key approximation error.
The folded, post-training method requires no runtime reconstruction or specialized kernels and outperforms structured pruning across evaluated tasks.
At 50% KV-cache retention and 256K context, it reports 47.8% lower inference FLOPs, 1.79× higher throughput, 43.2% lower TTFT, and 28.1% lower allocated GPU memory versus an uncompressed model.
papers.selection_reason: RoPE-compatible KV-cache compression reduces memory and inference FLOPs, fitting efficient attention and cache efficiency.
papers.title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies
papers.tldr: RACE compresses attention heads by selecting RoPE-compatible rotary pairs using joint query-key activation energy, reducing KV-cache memory and inference computation without runtime reconstruction.

papers.abstract: Latent diffusion models have recently achieved remarkable progress in Real-world Image Super-Resolution (Real-SR). However, existing methods consistently exhibit a persistent seesaw effect: enhancing perceptual realism compromises structural fidelity. This effect, we argue, is not intrinsic to diffusion models, but largely stems from the architectural constraints of prevailing two-stage frameworks. To address this challenge, we propose PixelSR, a novel single-stage Pixel Diffusion Transformer for Real-SR that operates directly in pixel space. Specifically, PixelSR consists of two core designs: Pixel-space Conditional Diffusion and Orthogonal Flow Decoupling. The former establishes an effective pixel-space restoration framework by integrating spatially aligned LR conditioning, visual semantic guidance, and lightweight texture refinement, thereby bypassing VAE compression and enabling end-to-end optimization directly in RGB space. Complementarily, the latter decomposes the asymmetric flow target into a low-rank semantic component and a noise-free orthogonal texture component. By routing these components to specialized branches, it achieves decoupled optimization with reduced mutual interference. Benefiting from these designs, our PixelSR restores perceptually realistic details while faithfully preserving structural content. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that PixelSR not only achieves competitive performance, but also effectively mitigates the fidelity--realism seesaw effect.
authors: Xiang Lv, Kai Zhao, Qiang Wang, Qiao Mo, Chao Zhou, Mingwen Shao
bullets: Targets the realism–fidelity trade-off attributed to architectural limitations in two-stage diffusion frameworks.
Uses pixel-space conditional diffusion with aligned low-resolution conditioning, semantic guidance, and lightweight texture refinement.
Introduces Orthogonal Flow Decoupling to separate low-rank semantic and orthogonal texture components into specialized branches.
Avoids VAE compression and enables end-to-end optimization directly in RGB space.
Experiments across multiple benchmarks show competitive performance and mitigation of the fidelity–realism seesaw effect.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a pixel-space diffusion transformer and orthogonal flow decoupling for super-resolution, offering a novel approach to diffusion efficiency and architecture.
papers.title: PixelSR: Pixel-Space Orthogonal Flow Decoupling for Real-World Image Super-Resolution
papers.tldr: PixelSR is a single-stage pixel-space diffusion transformer designed to improve Real-SR perceptual detail without sacrificing structural fidelity.

papers.abstract: Sparse attention limits the keys used by each query, but finding those keys can still require a full-prefix scan at every layer. We introduce \textbf{MLIPS (Multi-Layer Indexer Pool Sharing)}, a training-free method that shares candidate search while retaining each consumer's own scoring and selection. A producer publishes a top-$M$ pool larger than the attention budget $K$; subsequent layers select their own top-$K$ from that pool. Measurements across three sparse-attention model families show substantially higher coverage from broad pools than overlap between final selections. We implement layerwise sharing, persistent decode reuse, and a coarse producer in vLLM for DeepSeek-V4-Flash. Across four long-context suites, three consumer layers per producer give $1.14$--$1.40\times$ speedups and $14.8$--$27.4\%$ lower GPU energy, with observed accuracy changes of $-1.49$ to $+0.29$ percentage points in single runs. More extensive sharing exposes task-dependent quality losses. Sampled prefill traces also reveal recurring selected KV positions across query groups and layers. We characterize this shared working-set structure and use it to motivate Top-$G$, an exploratory bounded pool construction for prefill. Its deployment, task accuracy, and serving benefits remain open.
authors: Samkit Jain, Sai Kishan Pampana, Shlok Agarwal
bullets: Sparse attention still incurs costly full-prefix key searches at every layer.
A producer publishes a top-M candidate pool; each consumer independently selects its own top-K keys.
Implemented in vLLM for DeepSeek-V4-Flash, sharing three consumer layers per producer improved serving efficiency across four long-context suites.
Single-run accuracy changes ranged from −1.49 to +0.29 percentage points; more aggressive sharing can reduce quality.
Recurring KV-position reuse motivates Top-G, an exploratory prefill method whose deployment and benefits remain open.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free sharing of sparse-attention candidate search improves long-context LLM serving efficiency and GPU energy.
papers.title: MLIPS: Multi-Layer Indexer Pool Sharing
papers.tldr: MLIPS accelerates sparse attention by sharing broad candidate-key pools across layers, achieving 1.14–1.40× speedups with 14.8–27.4% lower GPU energy but task-dependent quality trade-offs.

papers.abstract: We propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, a novel update rule for associative matrix memories. KronLSTM extends the xLSTM family with a memory-revision mechanism that corrects targeted associations while modifying the memory only along a single direction in matrix space. This minimally invasive memory revision reduces interference with previously stored information compared with delta-rule updates, making it particularly well suited for long-context language modeling. The resulting memory dynamics can be mathematically described as a Markov chain that converges to a steady-state distribution, while the expected norm of the memory matrix remains uniformly bounded throughout the entire input sequence. Hence, KronLSTM ensures stable memory dynamics without requiring additional normalization and stabilization mechanisms for the memory state. Experiments show that KronLSTM is competitive with, and often outperforms, existing linear attention architectures, including models of the (Gated) DeltaNet family, with particularly strong performance on long context benchmarks. These results establish the Kronecker Delta Rule as an effective and analytically tractable foundation for stable associative memory in recurrent linear attention architectures. Our code (https://github.com/NX-AI/KronLSTM) and models (https://huggingface.co/collections/NX-AI/kronlstm) are open-source.
authors: Anamaria-Roberta Hartl, Levente Z\'olyomi, Michael List, G\"unter Klambauer, Sebastian B\"ock, Sepp Hochreiter
bullets: Extends the xLSTM family with memory revision that corrects targeted associations along a single matrix-space direction.
Reduces interference with stored information compared with standard delta-rule updates.
Its memory dynamics form a convergent Markov chain with uniformly bounded expected memory norm, without extra stabilization or normalization.
Experiments find performance competitive with or often better than linear attention baselines, especially on long-context benchmarks.
Code and pretrained models are publicly available.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, offering stable memory dynamics and improved efficiency for long-context language modeling.
papers.title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention
papers.tldr: KronLSTM introduces a minimally invasive Kronecker Delta Rule for stable, high-performing long-context linear attention.

papers.abstract: Hybrid architectures offer a promising approach to efficient language modeling by combining a small number of full-attention layers with a larger number of efficient sequence layers, such as sparse attention and recurrent layers. While full-attention layers maintain a KV cache that grows linearly with sequence length, efficient layers typically rely on separate, fixed-size states rather than accessing this richer existing memory. Recent work has begun exploring ways to allow efficient layers access to the KV cache, but the theoretical benefits of such access, and the extent to which existing approaches can realize them remain poorly understood. We investigate these questions by analyzing the expressive power of individual hybrid blocks on function composition, a well-studied task in sequence-model expressivity associated with multi-hop reasoning. We first establish that both conventional hybrid blocks and those with top-$\kappa$ KV-cache access require $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$ capacity to compute even two-function composition over a domain of size $n$. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the \emph{Multi-hop Retrieval Attention} (MuRA) hybrid block, a simple architecture that enables multi-hop retrieval from a shared KV cache while preserving asymptotic computational and memory efficiency. We prove that a single fixed size $m$-hop MuRA block can compute $m$-function composition, whereas computing $(m+1)$-function composition with the same retrieval depth requires polynomial model size, establishing a strict expressivity hierarchy in retrieval depth. Synthetic experiments support this hierarchy, showing that increasing retrieval depth enables learning progressively deeper compositions, substantially outperforming existing hybrid architectures. Together, our results identify multi-hop retrieval as a promising mechanism for improving the expressive power of efficient hybrid architectures.
authors: Yam Eitan, Gilad Yehudai, Haggai Maron
bullets: Hybrid models combine a few full-attention layers with more efficient sparse-attention or recurrent layers, but efficient layers typically cannot exploit the full KV cache.
Conventional hybrid blocks and top-κ KV-cache access require Ω(√n) capacity even for two-function composition over a domain of size n.
The proposed Multi-hop Retrieval Attention (MuRA) block supports multi-hop access to a shared KV cache while preserving asymptotic computational and memory efficiency.
A fixed-size m-hop MuRA block can compute m-function composition, while computing (m+1)-function composition at the same depth requires polynomial model size.
Synthetic experiments support a retrieval-depth hierarchy, with deeper retrieval enabling progressively deeper compositions and outperforming existing hybrid architectures.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a multi-hop retrieval attention block for efficient hybrid language architectures, improving expressivity while preserving asymptotic efficiency.
papers.title: Improving the Expressive Power of Hybrid Sequence Models via Multi-Hop Retrieval
papers.tldr: Multi-hop retrieval substantially increases the expressive power of efficient hybrid sequence models, enabling deeper compositional reasoning with fixed-size retrieval depth.

papers.abstract: Standard self-attention compares tokens by similarity but does not account for how much of a past state survives to the present. We introduce Dynamical Kernel Attention (DKA), which derives attention from robust estimation of a latent state evolving under stochastic dynamics. As a past state decays toward equilibrium under the dynamics, the information it carries about the present vanishes, bounding the total evidence a head can draw. Unlike recency biases, DKA can abstain when relevant evidence is weak and guarantees a bounded error when old tokens are discarded. DKA preserves the parallel structure and computational cost of standard attention. We present the model and its theory; empirical evaluation is deferred to a subsequent version.
bullets: Standard self-attention measures similarity but ignores how much information from past states remains relevant to the present.
DKA derives attention by robustly estimating a latent state evolving under stochastic dynamics.
Information from past states decays toward equilibrium, limiting the total evidence an attention head can use.
Unlike simple recency biases, DKA can abstain when relevant evidence is weak and provides error guarantees when old tokens are discarded.
The abstract presents theory and the model; empirical evaluation is deferred to future work.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes an attention mechanism with bounded-error token discarding, directly relevant to efficient attention and token eviction.
papers.title: Dynamical Kernel Attention: Estimating the Present from a Record of the Past
papers.tldr: Dynamical Kernel Attention incorporates stochastic state dynamics into attention, enabling principled decay, abstention under weak evidence, and bounded error from discarding old tokens without added computational cost.

papers.abstract: Smartphone GUI agents complete tasks in mobile apps by repeatedly reading the screen and asking a model for the next action. Mobile neural processing units (NPUs) enable local execution, keeping screen contents on the phone, but model latency accumulates with every action. Hybrid linear attention models reduce memory requirements, yet reusing their recurrent state requires checkpoints at the appropriate input positions. Agent requests retain instructions but rewrite recent history, so checkpoint policies designed for chat continuation can miss reusable prefixes. Retaining rollback states for speculative decoding can also move prompt processing off the NPU's matrix unit, adding overhead that outweighs decoding savings on short action outputs. A loaded model can further hold the NPU awake between tasks. We present Tandem, a runtime for hybrid GUI agents on mobile NPUs. Tandem saves recurrent state where consecutive prompts diverge, allowing later requests to reuse previously processed context. It keeps most prefill on the matrix unit and produces rollback states through a short per-token tail. Its verification kernel reads each weight block once for all proposed tokens. Between request bursts, Tandem releases NPU power votes without unloading the model. We implement Tandem in llama.cpp and evaluate it on recorded agent interactions across two Snapdragon generations. On a Snapdragon 8 Elite, Tandem reduces per-step latency by 30% for text-based screen descriptions and 16% for screenshots relative to llama.cpp's fastest NPU configuration, reduces energy per text step by 33%, and lowers standby power with the model loaded from 0.76 to 0.22 W.
authors: Zhuomin Chen, Jingchao Ni, Xu Zheng, Yong Chen, Mo Sha, Wei Cheng, Dongsheng Luo
bullets: Targets latency and energy overhead from repeatedly processing evolving GUI-agent prompts on smartphones.
Saves recurrent states at prompt-divergence points so later requests can reuse shared context.
Keeps most prompt processing on the NPU matrix unit and generates rollback states with a short per-token tail.
Uses a verification kernel that reads each weight block once for all proposed tokens, and releases NPU power votes between request bursts.
On Snapdragon 8 Elite, reduces per-step latency by 30% for text descriptions and 16% for screenshots, cuts text-step energy by 33%, and lowers loaded-model standby power from 0.76 to 0.22 W.
papers.selection_reason: Runtime for hybrid linear-attention GUI agents on mobile NPUs; reduces latency and energy via recurrent-state checkpoint reuse and efficient verification.
papers.title: Tandem: Serving Hybrid Linear-Attention GUI Agents on Mobile NPUs
papers.tldr: Tandem is a mobile-NPU runtime that accelerates hybrid linear-attention GUI agents by reusing prompt state efficiently while reducing energy and standby power.

papers.abstract: Autoregressive Diffusion Transformers have emerged as a powerful paradigm for long video generation. However, they are often constrained by prohibitive computational overhead and substantial memory footprints. This inefficiency arises from dense computation mechanisms that allocate uniform processing resources across all spatiotemporal regions, failing to leverage the inherent temporal redundancy of video where motion is typically confined to sparse areas. In this paper, we propose Dynamics-Aware Sparse Attention (DASA), a unified framework that shifts from dense computation to sparse, motion-driven generation to eliminate both storage and computational redundancies. Inspired by video codec principles, our approach explicitly decouples video content into dynamic and static regions. To mitigate memory bottlenecks, we selectively compress the historical KV cache by retaining only dynamic features within the generated chunk. Furthermore, to reduce computational overhead, we employ a region-level computation allocation strategy based on localized dynamics. Additionally, a dynamics-guided distillation method is introduced to enhance performance via a lightweight distillation training process. Experiments on VBench demonstrate that our approach accelerates autoregressive video generation by 2.16x, while preserving high visual fidelity.
authors: Yuanyu He, Zhuokun Chen, Yefei He, Zhiwei Tang, Jiasheng Tang, Yinghao Yu, Jianfei Cai, Bohan Zhuang
bullets: Addresses the high computational cost and memory usage of dense autoregressive video diffusion.
Separates dynamic and static regions to exploit temporal redundancy in videos.
Compresses historical KV caches by retaining dynamic features and allocates computation according to localized motion.
Uses dynamics-guided distillation to improve performance with lightweight training.
On VBench, achieves 2.16× faster generation while maintaining high visual fidelity.
papers.selection_reason: Directly targets efficient autoregressive video diffusion with sparse attention and KV cache compression, fitting efficient AI and video generation interests.
papers.title: Dynamics-Aware Sparse Attention for Efficient Autoregressive Video Diffusion
papers.tldr: DASA makes autoregressive video diffusion more efficient by focusing computation and memory on regions with motion while preserving visual quality.

papers.abstract: Diffusion transformers generate high-quality videos but remain computationally expensive. Sparse attention and temporal caching reduce computation within and across denoising steps, respectively, offering a natural composition. However, predictions produced with sparse attention become sources for temporal reuse, coupling their errors along the sampling trajectory. We observe that improving the accuracy of these sources recovers fidelity without changing the reuse schedule, and that sparsification errors remain directionally aligned across nearby steps, suggesting that correction information can be shared rather than recomputed. These observations motivate RECAP, a training-free method that couples sparse attention with hierarchical caching through reciprocal correction, adaptively coordinated by online error feedback. Cached dense refinement corrects omitted interactions in current sparse estimates, while fresh sparse statistics track input changes and regulate the aging correction. The resulting predictions then renew the sources for whole-step prediction reuse, allowing prediction history to advance between dense refreshes. We evaluate RECAP on multiple video diffusion models against sparse-attention methods, caching methods, and their direct compositions. On HunyuanVideo at 720p 5-second generation, RECAP achieves a 3.05x speedup and outperforms all tested direct compositions in both fidelity and inference speed.
authors: Tiange Xu, Kai Liu, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang
bullets: Addresses the computational cost of diffusion transformers for high-quality video generation.
Uses training-free reciprocal correction: cached dense refinement fixes sparse-attention omissions, while fresh sparse statistics monitor input changes.
Employs online error feedback to coordinate sparse attention, hierarchical caching, and correction aging without changing the reuse schedule.
Evaluated across multiple video diffusion models against sparse-attention, caching, and direct-composition baselines.
On HunyuanVideo at 720p for 5-second videos, reports a 3.05× speedup and better fidelity and speed than tested direct compositions.
papers.selection_reason: Directly addresses efficient video diffusion via sparse attention and hierarchical caching, fitting both efficient AI and video diffusion interests.
papers.title: RECAP: Reciprocal Sparse Attention and Hierarchical Caching for Efficient Video Diffusion
papers.tldr: RECAP accelerates video diffusion by combining sparse attention and hierarchical caching with reciprocal error correction, achieving faster and higher-fidelity generation than direct combinations of existing methods.

papers.abstract: Micro-expert pruning reduces the capacity of mixture-of-experts (MoE) models by removing coupled channels within routed experts. However, finer pruning granularity alone does not guarantee the preservation of downstream capabilities, as similar language-modeling perplexity can accompany substantially different task performance. We revisit micro-expert mask construction as two distinct decisions: allocating retained capacity across experts and selecting channels within that capacity. We propose UC-RAMP, a two-stage post-training pruning framework that explicitly separates these decisions. CAPE uses cross-domain calibration evidence to redistribute expert widths under an exact layer-wise budget, while RAMP refines channel composition at fixed widths through one-out, one-in exchanges guided by a channel-interaction surrogate. Across three MoE models at 25% and 50% routed-expert channel pruning, UC-RAMP achieves the highest ten-task mean accuracy among evaluated pruning methods in five of six settings. At 50% pruning, it outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline by 8.19, 3.96, and 6.14 percentage points across the three models, respectively. In a single-A100 deployment at 25% pruning, UC-RAMP reduces measured time to first token by 19.7--23.9% and time per output token by 20.2--22.3% relative to the unpruned model. The code is available at https://github.com/xzktx003/UC_RAMP.
authors: Zukang Xu, Xinpei Gao, Xing Hu, Zhe Jiang, Dawei Yang
bullets: Micro-expert pruning can maintain language-modeling perplexity yet degrade downstream tasks, motivating better mask construction.
CAPE redistributes retained expert widths using cross-domain calibration under exact layer-wise budgets.
RAMP refines channel selection at fixed widths via one-out, one-in exchanges guided by channel interactions.
Across three MoE models and two pruning levels, UC-RAMP achieved the best mean accuracy in five of six settings.
At 25% pruning, it reduced single-A100 time to first token by 19.7–23.9% and time per output token by 20.2–22.3% versus the unpruned model.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes UC-RAMP, a two-stage pruning framework for Mixture-of-Experts models that separates expert width allocation from channel selection to improve efficiency and accuracy.
papers.title: Fine-Grained Units, Flat Decisions: Hierarchical Micro-Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Models
papers.tldr: UC-RAMP improves MoE pruning by separately reallocating capacity across experts and selecting channels within each expert, preserving task performance while reducing inference latency.

papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) are becoming a powerful alternative to conventional tabular learning, adapting to new datasets in context without task-specific training.
