Current architectures, however, face a trade-off: models that preserve cell-level representations are expensive because they repeatedly attend across rows and columns, while faster models collapse each row into a fixed embedding and lose this fine-grained state. We introduce Factorized Tabular Foundation Models (FTFM), which preserve cell representations while factorizing their computation through one contextual latent per row and one per column. Cells no longer attend to one another directly; instead, each cell is updated through the interaction of its row and column latents, reducing repeated attention while retaining feature-specific information. FTFM achieves competitive predictive performance in tabular classification on major benchmarks such as TabArena and BeyondArena.
bullets: Existing TFMs either incur high costs from repeated row- and column-wise attention or lose detail by compressing each row into one embedding.
FTFM assigns one contextual latent to each row and each column.
Cells interact indirectly through their corresponding row and column latents rather than attending to one another directly.
The approach retains feature-specific cell representations while reducing repeated attention computation.
FTFM achieves competitive tabular-classification performance on benchmarks including TabArena and BeyondArena.
papers.selection_reason: Factorized computation via row/column latents reduces repeated attention; efficiency idea transferable to efficient attention mechanisms.
papers.title: FTFM: Factorized Tabular Foundation Models
papers.tldr: FTFM preserves fine-grained cell information in tabular foundation models while reducing computation through factorized row and column latents.

papers.abstract: We introduce ReDT, a feed-forward visual geometry transformer designed to scale multi-view reconstruction to high-definition (HD) inputs. Existing visual geometry transformers are typically trained at fixed, standard definition (SD) resolutions and exhibit degraded reconstruction quality and poor computational scaling to high input resolutions. While recent efficient architectures reduce the complexity of inter-frame attention, expensive intra-frame and encoder attention remain largely unaddressed, making HD reconstruction impractical with existing architectures. ReDT addresses both limitations with a resolution-aware architecture designed to scale to high-resolution inputs. The key idea of ReDT is to first map each view to a fixed-size set of basis tokens, compute correspondences in this compact constant-size basis space, and then project the outputs back to the original resolution for dense prediction. By decoupling the internal representation from input resolution during attention, ReDT substantially reduces the computational cost of high-resolution 3D reconstruction and improves model performance at all resolutions. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets spanning SD to FHD (2K) show that ReDT outperforms state-of-the-art visual geometry transformers in both reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. For instance, on the ETH3D (2K) dataset, ReDT achieves a $16\times$ speedup, a $34\%$ reduction in peak GPU memory usage, and a $33\%$ reduction in chamfer distance over VGGT-$\Omega$. \href{https://redt.github.io}{Project Website.}
authors: Abteen Arab, Guile Wu, Dongfeng Bai
bullets: Existing visual geometry transformers scale poorly to HD inputs because intra-frame and encoder attention remain expensive.
ReDT maps each view to a fixed-size set of basis tokens, computes correspondences in this compact space, and projects results back for dense prediction.
Experiments across SD to FHD (2K) datasets show improved reconstruction quality and computational efficiency at all tested resolutions.
On ETH3D at 2K, ReDT reports 16× faster inference, 34% lower peak GPU memory, and 33% lower Chamfer distance than VGGT-Ω.
papers.selection_reason: Resolution-decoupled visual geometry transformer for efficient HD multi-view reconstruction; fits 3D foundation models and efficient attention.
papers.title: ReDT: Resolution-Decoupled Visual Geometry Transformer
papers.tldr: ReDT enables efficient high-resolution multi-view 3D reconstruction by decoupling attention computation from input resolution.

papers.abstract: To determine where computation is needed in volumetric segmentation networks, we analyze block-level redundancy and stage-wise token-mixer contribution. Centered Kernel Alignment reveals high input-output representational similarity within blocks of representative convolutional, hybrid, and Transformer-style segmentation networks. Similarity-guided pruning reduces their parameter counts by 39-75% while decreasing mean Dice by less than 0.4 percentage points. To examine token mixers within blocks, we introduce Anatomical Relation Distortion, which quantifies how bypassing a mixer distorts feature relations between labeled anatomical positions. Applied to an unpruned candidate architecture, Centered Kernel Alignment indicates high representational redundancy in intermediate encoder mixers, whereas Anatomical Relation Distortion shows that they contribute little and the bottleneck mixer most. These findings motivate SlimFormer++, which uses Selective Mixing blocks with windowed Mamba mixing in the first encoder stage and only residual channel MLPs in deeper stages. At the bottleneck, Augmented Mixing injects similarity-weighted sparse long-range context into the axial taps of a depthwise convolution at cost linear in voxel count. Evaluated against 12 baselines across eight public CT, MRI, and ultrasound datasets (1,809 cases), SlimFormer++ achieves the highest mean Dice (87.84%) and lowest mean HD95 (6.50 mm) with the fewest parameters (5.98 million). These results support stage-aware token mixing as a design strategy for improving the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in volumetric segmentation. The source code is available at https://github.com/WHHHHHY822/SlimFormerPlusPlus
authors: Yang Hong, Lei Zhang, Zhihong Liu, Jianqing Mo, Xujiong Ye
bullets: Block-level redundancy analysis shows 39–75% parameter pruning can reduce mean Dice by less than 0.4 percentage points.
Anatomical Relation Distortion indicates early and intermediate encoder mixers contribute little, while bottleneck mixing is most important.
The model uses windowed Mamba mixing early, residual channel MLPs in deeper stages, and augmented sparse long-range mixing at the bottleneck.
Across eight public CT, MRI, and ultrasound datasets, it reports 87.84% mean Dice and 6.50 mm mean HD95 with 5.98M parameters.
The findings support stage-aware token mixing as a strategy for efficient volumetric segmentation.
papers.selection_reason: Efficient volumetric segmentation via block pruning and selective token mixing; fits efficient attention and 3D perception.
papers.title: SlimFormer++: Token Mixing Where It Matters for Efficient 3D Medical Image Segmentation
papers.tldr: SlimFormer++ improves the accuracy–efficiency trade-off in 3D medical image segmentation by concentrating token mixing where it matters most.

papers.abstract: Traffic forecasting models based on spectral graph convolution offer an interpretable account of how information is mixed between sensors, but they rely on an eigendecomposition of the graph Laplacian. It costs cubic time, is fixed by the road network, and provides a symmetric operator that cannot represent the directed propagation of traffic congestion. Attention-based spatio-temporal transformers remove these limitations but generate a dense sensor-by-sensor attention map at each layer and time step, so memory, rather than accuracy, becomes the binding constraint on large networks. We introduce the spectral adaptive graph transformer, whose spatial operator is learned rather than derived from the Laplacian, directed rather than symmetric, and conditioned on the current traffic state rather than a static state, at a cost linear in the number of sensors. A sparse road graph diffusion branch provides the strictly local propagation that a low-rank operator cannot express, and a zero-initialized gate learns the balance between the two. Before spatial mixing, a unit-mean-gain frequency-bin attention module reweights each sensor's short-term periodicities according to its identity and current context. Across six public benchmarks spanning 170 to 1843 sensors, evaluated over three random seeds, the proposed model attains the lowest error of any single end-to-end model on one benchmark and remains competitive with the strongest current attention models on the others, while using about a quarter of their memory and training about twice as fast.
authors: Amirhossein Ghaffari, Susanna Pirttikangas, Ekaterina Gilman
bullets: Addresses cubic eigendecomposition costs, static symmetric propagation, and dense attention memory demands.
Learns a directed, traffic-state-conditioned spatial operator with linear scaling in the number of sensors.
Combines low-rank global propagation with sparse road-graph diffusion through a zero-initialized balancing gate.
Reweights each sensor’s short-term periodicities using context- and identity-dependent frequency-bin attention.

Across six benchmarks, achieves the best single-model error on one benchmark, competitive results elsewhere, about one-quarter the memory use, and roughly twice the training speed of strong attention models.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a learned low-rank spatial operator plus sparse diffusion to replace dense attention, reducing memory and compute for spatio-temporal forecasting.
papers.title: Spectral Adaptive Graph Transformer for Efficient and Scalable Traffic Forecasting
papers.tldr: A scalable traffic forecasting transformer replaces costly spectral decomposition and dense attention with state-adaptive directed low-rank mixing plus sparse local diffusion, reducing resource use while maintaining competitive accuracy.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) promises instant scene reconstruction with high-quality novel-view synthesis. Yet, fine-grained geometry and appearance remain difficult to recover, motivating us to revisit how feed-forward models represent, aggregate, and refine detailed visual information. We introduce FineSplat, a feed-forward 3DGS framework built around fine-grained image patches. Since global multi-view attention becomes prohibitively expensive at such high token resolutions, we develop a dual-grouping strategy that combines two complementary forms of locality: view-wise grouping enables efficient interaction among neighboring views, while 3D spatial grouping reconnects geometrically related tokens that may never have interacted under view-wise grouping by lifting them into the 3D scene space. We further leverage reconstruction error as direct feedback, providing an explicit rendering-based signal to recover fine-grained structures and appearance, thereby overcoming the limitations of one-pass feed-forward prediction. Finally, a compact Gaussian generation scheme preserves the benefits of fine-grained features without unnecessarily increasing the number of primitives. Together, these designs enable FineSplat to recover richer geometry and appearance while remaining efficient and compact, achieving state-of-the-art results by a substantial margin, under the same or smaller Gaussian budgets than existing methods.
authors: Hyebin Kim, Hwasik Jeong, Joonhyuk Park, Gyeongjin Kang, Jungwoo Kim, Younghyun Kim, Eunbyung Park
bullets: Targets the difficulty of recovering fine-grained geometry and appearance in feed-forward 3DGS.
Uses view-wise grouping for efficient neighboring-view interaction and 3D spatial grouping to reconnect geometrically related tokens.
Uses rendering reconstruction error as explicit feedback to refine structures and appearance beyond one-pass prediction.
Generates a compact set of Gaussians to retain fine-detail benefits without unnecessarily increasing primitive counts.
Reports state-of-the-art performance by a substantial margin under the same or smaller Gaussian budgets, according to the abstract.
papers.selection_reason: Feed-forward 3DGS with dual-grouping attention and compact Gaussian generation; relevant to 3D reconstruction and efficient attention.
papers.title: FineSplat: Fine Patches, Local Groups, Detailed Splats
papers.tldr: FineSplat improves feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting by combining fine image patches, local view/3D grouping, reconstruction-error feedback, and compact Gaussian generation.

papers.abstract: Sparse attention speeds up long-context decoding by reading few keys of the KV cache, but existing methods do not control the error of a query, and on real KV caches their errors have heavy tails. We show that perturbing the score of every key with an independent Exp(1) variable turns threshold retrieval into sampling keys with probability proportional to their attention weights. Lowering the threshold along a geometric grid gives nested samples, a Horvitz--Thompson estimate of the output at every level, and confidence bounds that hold simultaneously over all levels, so each head stops at the first level whose certificate meets the target error $\varepsilon$. With fresh perturbations at every decoding step, each certificate fails with probability at most $\delta$ during generation. At a suitable threshold, the estimator reads $O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\delta))$ values regardless of the context length, and no adaptive method reads fewer, up to constants. A 4-bit scan with deterministic bounds, shared across a grouped-query-attention group, generates the candidates exactly but reads every key. On three LLMs and ten settings at 16K--128K tokens, no certificate is violated, and at equal keys read our 90th-percentile error is 4.6--7.9$\times$ lower than that of the best of 15 baseline families. At equal bytes, the best baselines have 0.6--1.6 times our 90th-percentile error and at least 4.9 times our largest. End to end, our method stays within one point of dense attention on tasks and within 0.1\% in PG-19 perplexity, and the strongest baselines at equal bytes score as well. On CPU, decoding steps at 32K--128K tokens run 1.1--1.4$\times$ faster than dense attention on the same 16-bit cache.
bullets: Perturbing key scores with independent Exp(1) noise converts threshold retrieval into sampling proportional to attention weights.
Nested samples across thresholds enable Horvitz–Thompson output estimates and simultaneous confidence certificates.
Each head stops when its estimated error is below ε; with fresh perturbations, certificate failure is bounded by δ during generation.
The estimator needs O(ε⁻² log(1/δ)) reads, independent of context length, and this read complexity is optimal up to constants.
Across 16K–128K contexts, certificates were never violated; decoding was 1.1–1.4× faster than dense attention on CPU while maintaining near-dense task quality.
papers.selection_reason: Certified sparse attention with perturbed retrieval reduces KV-cache reads for long-context decoding, fitting efficient attention and long-context model interests.
papers.title: Certified Sparse Attention via Perturbed Retrieval
papers.tldr: Certified Sparse Attention uses perturbed retrieval and adaptive sampling to provide high-probability error guarantees while reading far fewer KV-cache values during long-context decoding.

papers.abstract: On AWS Trainium2, every component of a diffusion model runs as a program compiled ahead of time for fixed shapes, while pipelines differ across models, prompt lengths across requests, and caching decisions across denoising steps. We present Difflet, a serving engine in which five model pipelines share one compilation backend, joint attention is split across cores by attention head, and a host controller decides at each denoising step whether to run the denoiser or reuse its earlier output. A small probe program computes the caching signal on the device and returns one number per step, and a resident model process keeps every program loaded across requests. Across five image and video model families, fused attention accelerates denoiser steps by 1.2-4.3x over the same framework using PyTorch/XLA attention, and at 32.8k visual tokens it is the only attention that compiles. On four of the five models, resident serving is 1.5-3.4x faster than standalone runs that reload weights from a warm file cache for each generation.
authors: Bin Ma, Min Yu, Vijay Kodamalla, Jialin Liu, Dong Li
bullets: Addresses fixed-shape compilation constraints across varying pipelines, prompt lengths, and denoising-time caching decisions.
Uses one compilation backend for five pipelines, splits joint attention across cores by head, and fuses attention computation.
A host controller selectively reuses denoiser outputs, guided by a device-side probe that produces one caching signal per step.
Fused attention is 1.2–4.3× faster than PyTorch/XLA attention and is the only attention variant compiling at 32.8k visual tokens.
Resident serving is 1.5–3.4× faster than reloading weights for each generation on four of five models.
papers.selection_reason: Presents Difflet, a fast inference engine for diffusion transformer models on AWS Trainium, optimizing attention computation and caching to improve serving efficiency.
papers.title: DIFFLET: A Fast Inference Engine for Diffusion Transformer Models on AWS Trainium
papers.tldr: Difflet speeds diffusion-transformer inference on AWS Trainium2 through shared compilation, fused attention, adaptive caching, and resident model serving.

papers.abstract: Long-context decoding in large language models (LLMs) is increasingly bottlenecked by the memory and computation required to attend over an ever-growing Key-Value (KV) cache at each autoregressive step. Although token-level sparse attention reduces this burden by restricting computation to a small subset of relevant past tokens, its practical gains are often offset by repeatedly recomputing layer-wise sparse indices as the context grows. A common remedy is to share sparse indices across layers by computing them only at designated anchor layers, but such static reuse ignores the layer-wise evolution of attention patterns, causing the reused indices to progressively deviate from the layer-specific optima and incur substantial attention loss. By revisiting cross-layer sparsity from the perspective of attention dynamics, we find that inter-layer salient token shift is highly localized: although the exact top-$\kappa$ indices differ across layers, the core high-attention tokens remain stable, with changes concentrated near the expanded boundary of previously selected regions. Motivated by this, we propose Prism Attention, a proposal-refined sparse attention framework. It replaces rigid cross-layer index reuse with a coarse-to-fine strategy, preserving layer-wise adaptability while retaining the efficiency benefits of cross-layer sharing. Extensive experiments show that Prism Attention achieves state-of-the-art performance among mainstream sparse attention methods on both reasoning and long-context benchmarks, while attaining a $3.4\times$ end-to-end decoding speedup over FlashAttention at 128K context length.
authors: Zhenxu Tian, Kebin Liu, Zhengwu Yang, Yi Su, Qingqing Dang, Yanlin Sha, Kaipeng Deng, Dianhai Yu, Yanjun Ma, Juntao Li, Min Zhang
bullets: Long-context decoding is bottlenecked by repeated attention over the growing KV cache.
Static cross-layer index sharing is efficient but can lose accuracy as attention patterns evolve across layers.
The method observes that salient-token changes are localized near the boundaries of previously selected regions.
Its coarse-to-fine proposal-refinement strategy preserves layer adaptability while reducing index recomputation.
It reports state-of-the-art performance among mainstream sparse-attention methods and a 3.4× decoding speedup over FlashAttention at 128K context.
papers.selection_reason: Sparse attention with cross-layer index sharing reduces KV-cache memory and decoding compute.
papers.title: Prism Attention: Proposal-Refined Index Sharing Mechanism for Efficient LLMs Inference
papers.tldr: Prism Attention accelerates long-context LLM decoding by refining shared sparse-attention indices across layers instead of rigidly reusing them.

papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have become a common backbone for high-quality text-to-image and text-to-video generation, but repeated dense self-attention remains a major inference bottleneck as token sequences grow and the same operator is invoked across many denoising steps. Our study suggests that dense attention in pretrained DiTs contains reusable layer/head-specific high-mass structure that can be identified from a small offline calibration set and reused across future generations. This leads to Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention, a train-free attention replacement that reuses static sink masks and supplements them with a lightweight pooled-KV branch, while leaving model weights and sampling schedules unchanged. On Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, the method attains 1.54$\times$ end-to-end speedup while maintaining generation quality. On Z-Image-Turbo, it attains 1.57$\times$ end-to-end speedup with competitive GenEval2 performance. These results indicate that reusable importance-aware sparse support can provide an effective train-free acceleration path for both T2V and T2I DiTs.
authors: Bingxin Xing, Yu Zhang, Jiatong Ding, Lei Lu, Ping Wang
bullets: Targets the inference cost of repeated dense self-attention in DiTs with long token sequences and many denoising steps.
Uses small offline calibration to identify reusable, layer/head-specific high-mass attention structure.
Combines static sink masks with a lightweight pooled-KV branch as a train-free attention replacement.
Achieves 1.54× end-to-end speedup on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B while maintaining generation quality.
Achieves 1.57× end-to-end speedup on Z-Image-Turbo with competitive GenEval2 performance; scope covers T2V and T2I DiTs.
papers.selection_reason: Train-free sparse attention replacement for efficient T2I/T2V diffusion transformers.
papers.title: Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention for Efficient Inference in T2I/T2V Diffusion Transformers
papers.tldr: Sink-Sparse Hybrid Attention accelerates pretrained text-to-image and text-to-video diffusion Transformers by reusing calibrated sparse attention structure without retraining or changing sampling schedules.

papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a powerful machine learning framework that allows building a global model from the contributions of multiple, distributed clients, while ensuring the privacy of their local data. However, its heavy computational and communication overheads challenge its use for contemporary AI workloads such as natural language processing (NLP) and multimodal analysis. For this reason, this paper presents a novel small language model that leverages byte-level text and multimodal data processing, enhanced by a linear attention mechanism, to enable manageable Federated Learning of NLP and multimodal analysis tasks. The proposed model, nicknamed FederatedBytes, manages to process text and any other data types, including images, by treating its input as a mere sequence of bytes, while its lean linear attention mechanism allows abating the overall memory and computational footprint. To prove the effectiveness of the proposed model we have carried out an extensive performance evaluation on sentiment analysis tasks in multilingual and multimodal settings over the Multilingual Amazon Reviews and ScienceQA datasets. The experimental results show that FederatedBytes has been able to outperform comparable models such as ByT5 and LSTM, achieving higher accuracy while significantly reducing memory and communication overheads.
authors: Ali Sarabadani, Massimo Piccardi, Mehran Abolhasan, Farzad Tofigh, Ian Zhou, Justin Lipman
bullets: Targets the computational and communication costs that hinder federated NLP and multimodal learning.
Processes text, images, and other modalities uniformly as byte sequences, without tokenization.
Uses lean linear attention to reduce memory and computational requirements.
Evaluated on multilingual and multimodal sentiment analysis using Multilingual Amazon Reviews and ScienceQA.
The abstract reports higher accuracy than ByT5 and LSTM, alongside substantially lower memory and communication overheads.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a tokenizer-free, byte-level small language model for efficient federated learning, utilizing linear attention to reduce memory and computational footprint.
papers.title: FederatedBytes: Tokenizer-Free, Byte-Level Small Language Models for Efficient Multimodal Federated Learning
papers.tldr: FederatedBytes is a tokenizer-free, byte-level small language model using linear attention to make multimodal federated learning more efficient while maintaining strong sentiment-analysis performance.

papers.abstract: Augmenting softmax attention with forget gates typically relies on summing decay contributions along the key--query path. Because such accumulation is monotonic, these mechanisms cannot selectively erase intermediate context while preserving older, structurally relevant tokens. We propose First Passage Attention (FPA), which shifts from path summation to path extrema by lowering a key's logit proportionally to the deepest dip of a learned scalar field below that key's level over the intervening span. FPA encompasses the Forgetting Transformer (FoX) as a special case, and when the field and levels follow a shared learned walk, the alive keys with unpenalised logits naturally form a stack. We show that a constant-dimension FPA head realises any subset of keys left alive by subsequent dips, whereas softmax heads with positional biases or token-level forget gates require a head dimension linear in the number of keys. In synthetic experiments, one-layer FPA heads converge to these target sets while comparable softmax and FoX baselines fail on every seed. Scaling to a 110M-parameter language model, FPA matches FoX in perplexity and uniquely achieves perfect passkey retrieval at $8\times$ the training length, even with its key--value cache compressed to about $25\%$.
bullets: Addresses the limitation of monotonic decay mechanisms that cannot erase intermediate tokens selectively.
Uses path extrema: logits are penalized according to the deepest dip of a learned scalar field across the key–query span.
Includes the Forgetting Transformer as a special case; under a shared learned walk, unpenalized keys form a stack.
A constant-dimensional FPA head can realize arbitrary subsets of surviving keys, unlike comparable softmax-based mechanisms requiring dimension linear in key count.
In experiments, FPA converges to target key sets, matches FoX perplexity, and achieves perfect passkey retrieval at 8× training length with a cache compressed to about 25%.
papers.selection_reason: Novel attention mechanism with forget gates and KV cache compression, directly relevant to efficient attention and memory.
papers.title: First Passage Attention
papers.tldr: First Passage Attention enables selective forgetting of intermediate context while preserving older relevant tokens, outperforming comparable mechanisms on synthetic memory tasks and long-context passkey retrieval.

papers.abstract: Large language models can produce fluent answers that the supplied context does not support. A compact frozen proxy model can detect such answers by reading the context and another model's response, even from a proprietary generator. Attention-based detectors use summary statistics of the proxy's attention weights, but standard pipelines materialize the attention matrix, whose memory grows quadratically with sequence length. We compute these statistics without materializing attention, by accumulation in the FlashAttention pass, sparse lookups after it, or a second tiled pass over the scores, and classify them by this path into nearly free and costlier ones. On an H100, the statistics of five published detectors add 16% to the latency of a Qwen3-8B forward at 2K tokens, falling to 1.4% at 35K, and store 22.5 KiB per response token. On three benchmarks, probes trained on frozen Qwen3 proxies of 0.6B to 8B parameters prove strong detectors: a 4B proxy outperforms the strongest of nine zero-shot 4-9B LLM judges in F1 on two of the three, the proxies match or outperform specialized grounding checkers of up to 7B parameters, probing each proxy beats prompting it as a judge, and adding attention features significantly improves F1 in half of the 12 benchmark-proxy pairs, never significantly lowering it.
authors: Andrei Volodichev, Maksim Savichev, Nikita Sviridov, Artem Yuliy, Dmitry Simakov, Alexey Zaytsev
bullets: Targets unsupported but fluent LLM answers, including responses from proprietary generators.
Computes attention statistics during FlashAttention, via sparse lookups, or with a second tiled score pass, avoiding quadratic memory materialization.
On an H100, five detectors add 16% latency at 2K tokens and 1.4% at 35K, using 22.5 KiB per response token.
Across three benchmarks, frozen Qwen3 probes are strong detectors; a 4B proxy beats nine zero-shot LLM judges on two benchmarks and matches or exceeds specialized checkers.
Attention features significantly improve F1 in 6 of 12 benchmark–proxy pairs and never significantly reduce it.
papers.selection_reason: Computes attention statistics without materializing the attention matrix, reducing memory and latency for attention-based detectors.
papers.title: FlashAttention with Statistics: Low-Overhead Attention Features for Compact Hallucination Detectors
papers.tldr: FlashAttention-based computation makes attention features practical for compact, frozen-model hallucination detectors without storing the full attention matrix.

papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) dominate video generation but suffer from high inference cost due to the quadratic complexity of self-attention. Sparse attention mitigates this by skipping unnecessary computation in the attention matrix, but existing methods apply a fixed sparsity ratio throughout denoising and struggle to accurately determine which computations to skip. To address these limitations, we analyze attention dynamics through attention entropy and mean attention distance, and find that attention becomes increasingly concentrated across denoising steps. We further observe that blocks selected early continue to capture a large fraction of the total attention weight at later steps. These findings suggest two acceleration opportunities: the sparsity ratio should grow as denoising progresses, and earlier search results can be reused to reduce the search space. Based on these findings, we propose Growing Sparsity and Reduced Search (GSRS), a training-free framework that retains more computation early and progressively reduces it later, while restricting subsequent searches to an early candidate set to reduce search overhead. GSRS adopts Top-p selection for adaptive sparsity control, supported by a precise evaluation scheme that computes exact attention weights within the FlashAttention computation at negligible overhead. Experiments on HunyuanVideo and Wan 2.1 validate that GSRS achieves 1.55$\times$--2.21$\times$ speedup while maintaining generation quality comparable to full attention.
authors: Yun Dai, Yuyun Chen, Jiarui Wen, Huiping Zhuang, Cen Chen, Ziqian Zeng
bullets: Video DiTs are slowed by quadratic self-attention, while fixed-sparsity methods poorly reflect changing attention patterns during denoising.
Attention becomes increasingly concentrated over denoising steps, and early-selected blocks retain much of the later attention weight.
GSRS is training-free: it keeps more computation early, reduces it progressively, and restricts later searches to an early candidate set.
Top-p selection provides adaptive sparsity, with exact attention-weight evaluation integrated into FlashAttention at negligible overhead.
Validated on HunyuanVideo and Wan 2.1, GSRS delivers 1.55×–2.21× speedup while maintaining quality comparable to full attention.
papers.selection_reason: Training-free sparse attention acceleration for video diffusion with growing sparsity and reduced search; relevant to efficient video generation.
papers.title: Sparse Attention for Video Generation Acceleration via Growing Sparsity and Reduced Search
papers.tldr: GSRS accelerates video diffusion Transformers by progressively increasing attention sparsity and reusing early search results, achieving 1.55×–2.21× speedups with comparable quality to full attention.

papers.abstract: Automating organizational work means answering many small typed questions about one piece of state (does this email need a reply, how urgent is it, who owns it) with probabilities good enough to act on without a human. The open typed-decision model we compare against, like a standard cross-encoder, answers each question with a separate pass over the input. We present Verdict-MQ, an open encoder that reads a case once and answers all of its questions: given identical retained state tokens after truncation (verified on every reported case), a structured attention mask makes the state encoding independent of the questions, keeps questions from influencing each other, and makes option order irrelevant by construction. On the typed-decisions benchmark, a 395M Verdict-MQ matches the soft gold labels significantly better than the released 421M Laya specialist on all five fresh seeds (KL 0.080 vs 0.117, Brier 0.045 vs 0.061), an advantage that survives per-system temperature scaling; its higher accuracy (0.801 vs 0.767) lies past the benchmark's own saturation point, so we read that margin as closer agreement with the benchmark's labelling teacher. On RACE, BoolQ and MultiRC, against a matched fine-tuned baseline it wins on MultiRC and loses on RACE and on BoolQ, where its training is unstable; we measure zero-shot references ourselves, including a closed general system (Jev) that beats every fine-tuned encoder. A controlled comparison measures what the shared state costs: giving each question its own question-aware copy of the state gains 0.9-3.5 points on RACE and MultiRC at 1.4-2.5x the per-case latency, and nothing measurable on typed decisions, with the invariance guarantees unchanged.
bullets: Structured attention makes state encoding independent of questions, prevents question interaction, and makes option order irrelevant.
On the typed-decisions benchmark, the 395M model beats the released 421M specialist on soft-label agreement and accuracy across five seeds.
Against a matched fine-tuned baseline, it wins on MultiRC but loses on RACE and BoolQ, where training is unstable.
Question-specific state copies improve RACE and MultiRC by 0.9–3.5 points at 1.4–2.5× latency, but show no measurable benefit on typed decisions.
The study also reports zero-shot references, including a closed general system that outperforms all fine-tuned encoders.
papers.selection_reason: Structured attention mask enables shared state encoding across many questions, reducing per-case latency.
papers.title: Verdict: Encode Once, Decide Many
papers.tldr: Verdict-MQ encodes each case once to answer many typed questions, improving typed-decision calibration and accuracy while trading some performance for lower repeated-processing cost on standard QA tasks.

papers.abstract: We expand the exponential kernel of attention into a truncated Taylor series of $n$ terms and factorize each term into a tensor-power inner product, which collapses the causal history into exactly $n$ recurrent states, each updated by one rank-one outer product per token and independent of context length $N$. The recursion is lossless with respect to the truncated kernel ($2.2 \times 10^{-16}$ in float64), and the states are additive across chunks ($5.7 \times 10^{-14}$), so prefill admits a parallel scan. Measured exponents are $t \propto N^{2.28}$ for softmax against $N^{0.91}$ for states, with a crossover at $N \approx 728$ and $20.8\times$ at $N = 8192$; per-token decoding latency is constant at $7.3\,\mu$s against $N^{1.04}$ for softmax, giving $76.0\times$ at $N = 65536$. Accuracy improves exponentially in $n$ while cost grows combinatorially, since the $m$-th state is $\binom{d+m-1}{m}$ wide---a bound confirmed by SVD---so the optimum is second order, $n = 3$, at $6.5 \times 10^{-4}$ error and $9{,}945$ elements per head. Query and key normalization is a prerequisite: without it the argument exceeds the convergence radius and adding terms stops helping.
bullets: Approximates the exponential attention kernel with n Taylor terms and tensor-power factorization.
Maintains exactly n recurrent states using one rank-one outer-product update per token, independent of context length.
States combine additively across chunks, enabling parallel-scan prefill and constant per-token decoding latency.
The method scales more favorably than softmax attention for long contexts, with reported speedups up to 20.8× in prefill and 76.0× in decoding.
State width grows combinatorially with order; second order (n = 3) is identified as optimal, while query/key normalization is required for convergence.
papers.selection_reason: Linear-time attention via Taylor expansion with fixed recurrent states.
papers.title: Expanding Attention: A Taylor-Series Route to Linear-Time Transformers with a Fixed Number of Recurrent States
papers.tldr: A truncated Taylor expansion replaces softmax attention with a fixed number of recurrent states, enabling linear-time sequence processing while exposing a cost–accuracy trade-off.

papers.abstract: Long-context decoding is limited by memory bandwidth, because every output token reads the KV cache of every layer. Sparse decoding reduces this cost by reading only part of the KV cache. We observe that the number of pages a query needs varies widely across KV heads, layers and steps. Fixed budgets are simple, but they are sized for demanding cases and tuned per workload; adaptive budgets follow this variation more flexibly, but existing designs pay for it with extra selection cost or training. At the kernel level, FlashAttention-3 (FA3) and FlashInfer are designed for rows of similar length: with page lists whose length differs per KV head, they either pad the lists (forfeiting much of the sparse saving), leave thread blocks unbalanced, or rely on a host-side plan that runs outside the CUDA graph. We propose MOIRA, a training-free sparse decode path in vLLM whose budget adapts per KV head and per layer. For every request, layer, KV head and step, a coverage rule keeps the smallest set of pages whose estimated attention mass reaches a fraction $γ$. A new kernel, self-planning attention, lets each thread block derive its own share of the work from the list lengths, so the whole decode step stays inside the CUDA graph. On an H200, at RULER's 128k context, MOIRA with $γ=0.99$ matches dense accuracy while reading about 30% of the pages and reduces the time per output token (TPOT) by 2.2-2.5$\times$ relative to dense FA3; with $γ=0.98$ it reduces TPOT by 2.7$\times$ and stays within the noise of dense. Under high serving load it raises throughput by up to 51%. These results suggest that a budget adapted per head and layer, paired with a kernel that keeps such budgets inside the CUDA graph, makes sparse decoding both flexible and fast.
bullets: Long-context decoding is memory-bandwidth-bound because each token accesses every layer’s KV cache.
MOIRA selects the smallest set of pages reaching a target attention-mass coverage per request, layer, KV head, and decoding step.
Its self-planning attention kernel handles variable page-list lengths without padding, imbalance, or host-side CUDA-graph breaks.
On an H200 with 128k-token contexts, it reads about 30% of pages at γ=0.99 and achieves 2.2–2.5× lower TPOT than dense FA3 while matching dense accuracy.
At γ=0.98, TPOT improves by 2.7× and serving throughput increases by up to 51%, according to the abstract.
papers.selection_reason: Sparse adaptive-budget KV-cache decoding for long-context LLMs; strong efficiency contribution.
papers.title: MOIRA: Mass-Oriented Indexing with Ragged Attention for Long-Context Decoding
papers.tldr: MOIRA enables fast, training-free long-context decoding by adaptively reading only the KV-cache pages needed by each layer and KV head while preserving dense-model accuracy.

papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average $3.16\times$ decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.
authors: Bohan Sun, Zunhai Su, Xialie Zhuang, Jianjin Li, Ngai Wong, Chuan-Wei Kuo
bullets: Addresses the mismatch between target hidden features and the contextual needs of later draft positions.
Uses learned per-position queries and a lightweight state reader to retrieve and fuse supplementary context via residual updates.
Reduces overhead with low-rank state reads and fused operators, building on DSpark’s parallel backbone and sequential prediction head.
Across seven math, code, and dialogue benchmarks, reports a 3.16× average speedup over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3.8-27B.
Outperforms DSpark on all benchmarks, with average throughput and acceptance-length gains of 7.97% and 8.50%, respectively.
papers.selection_reason: Speculative decoding using recurrent states in hybrid linear attention LLMs; directly relevant to efficient attention, memory-efficient inference, and LLM architecture.
papers.title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
papers.tldr: ReaDy accelerates speculative decoding in hybrid linear-attention LLMs by retrieving position-specific context from the target model’s recurrent states.

papers.abstract: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. We explain the success of CPLMs by showing that they partially mitigate the LM head gradient bottleneck through an alternative gradient path.
bullets: Transformers may copy from inputs inefficiently despite appearing naturally suited to copying.
CPLMs augment the standard language-modeling head with a lightweight Copy-Paste head.
The method improves training efficiency, downstream performance, and provides useful operating points for long-context and retrieval tasks.
Improvements hold across model scales from 135M to 1.7B parameters and across backbones, with negligible training and inference overhead.
The authors attribute the gains to an alternative gradient path that partially alleviates the LM-head gradient bottleneck.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a Copy-Paste head to explicitly model input copying in LLMs, improving training efficiency and long-context performance, which is relevant to LLM architectures and efficient attention.
papers.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
papers.tldr: Copy-Paste Language Models add a lightweight copy mechanism that improves in-context copying, efficiency, and downstream performance with negligible overhead.

papers.abstract: Tokenization is an essential preprocessing step in almost all large language models (LLMs). One of the most popular frameworks is BPE tokenization, which consists of special token segmentation, pretokenization, and byte-pair encoding (BPE). However, existing algorithms are sequential, with each stage only processing complete output from the previous stage. In order to reduce latency and memory footprints, recent works (Jiang and Gong, ICML 2026) (Li, Yang and Mamouras, ASPLOS 2026) (Mamouras, Li and Yang, PLDI 2026) have initiated the study of online algorithms for subroutines such as pretokenization and BPE with a goal of streaming input to output as the input arrives online. However, the search for efficient online tokenization remains open. In this work, we formalize and resolve online tokenization. We introduce the notion of delay for online tokenization which characterizes the extent to which the algorithm output lags behind the (possibly computationally intractable) optimum. We give a near-linear time algorithm with optimal delay (up to constant factors). We complement this algorithm with a conditional lower bound: unless $\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{NP}$, there is no polynomial time algorithm that beats the delay of our algorithm by more than a constant factor. We implement a practical variant for tokenizers from OpenAI's tiktoken and HuggingFace's tokenizers. We obtain a $7.9\times$-$34.8\times$ latency advantage (measured as time to first token) over tiktoken (as well as the recent gigatoken tokenizer) and our implementation maintains approximately constant memory usage independent of input size. Our implementation also achieves a $2.4\times$-$7.0\times$ improvement in throughput over tiktoken and $15.8\times$-$38.1\times$ over tokenizers.
bullets: Defines delay for online tokenization relative to an offline optimum, even when computing that optimum may be intractable.
Provides a near-linear-time online algorithm whose delay is optimal up to constant factors.
Shows conditionally that, unless P = NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can improve its delay by more than a constant factor.
A practical implementation for tiktoken and HuggingFace tokenizers achieves lower time-to-first-token, higher throughput, and approximately constant memory usage with respect to input size.
papers.selection_reason: Online tokenization with optimal delay improves LLM preprocessing latency/memory, fitting efficient AI methods.
papers.title: Online Tokenization with Optimal Delay in Linear Time
papers.tldr: The paper formalizes online tokenization and presents a near-linear-time algorithm with provably optimal output delay and strong practical latency and throughput gains.

papers.abstract: Sparse attention reduces the KV-cache traffic that dominates long-context LLM decoding, but practical methods largely operate at coarse granularity. Token-level selection offers finer control, yet presents two challenges: low-dimensional scoring may lose query--key structure needed for accurate ranking, while gathering scattered selected tokens can offset the resulting latency benefit. We introduce Joint Subspace Sparse Attention (JSSA) to address both challenges. For selection quality, JSSA learns a shared low-dimensional query--key subspace by minimizing token-score preservation error. We upper-bound the resulting non-convex objective with a tractable marginal objective that admits a closed-form spectral solution; direct refinement of the exact objective provides no measurable improvement in the tested settings. For execution efficiency, we develop a gather-free token-level indexed-attention kernel that supports distinct per-KV-head selections under the standard grouped-query attention (GQA) KV-cache layout. Across standard GQA, hybrid sliding-window/global attention, and Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) models, JSSA consistently remains close to full-KV accuracy while avoiding the substantial generation-length inflation and architecture-dependent failures observed with competing methods. On an NVIDIA B200 GPU, JSSA achieves up to $6.43\times$ the decoding throughput of full-KV attention at 128K context. JSSA achieves reasoning accuracy comparable to model-native DSA without model training and reaches 96--99\% of its decoding throughput even at 700B scale large models.
authors: Jiwon Song, Yoongon Kim, Jae-Joon Kim
bullets: Addresses low-dimensional token-ranking errors and the latency cost of gathering scattered KV-cache tokens.
Learns a shared query–key subspace via a tractable spectral objective for token selection.
Introduces a gather-free indexed-attention kernel supporting distinct selections per KV head under GQA.
Remains close to full-KV accuracy across GQA, hybrid sliding-window/global attention, and MLA models.
Matches model-native DSA reasoning accuracy without training and reaches 96–99% of its decoding throughput at 700B scale.
papers.selection_reason: Sparse attention for efficient long-context decoding; directly relevant to efficient attention and KV-cache reduction.
papers.title: Joint Subspace Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
papers.tldr: JSSA enables accurate, token-level sparse attention for long-context decoding while reducing KV-cache traffic and achieving up to 6.43× full-KV throughput at 128K context.

papers.abstract: Summary-token architectures such as Kwai Summary Attention (KSA) compress distant context into learnable Summary token per chunk, and hybrid variants interleave these layers with full attention to retain exact access to the original text. In such hybrid KSA-Full architecture, the interleaving inserted summary tokens are served as a streaming flow role across different layers. Although effective, however, it also introduce some bottlenecks: (1) the different layers summary compression chunk must be same, therefore hard to reach a flexible KV Cache compression, e.g., different layer set different summary compression chunk window. (2) in the full-attention layers, the summary token introduced additional computation cost, but such layer ignore them and still pay quadratic prefilling, therefore unfriendly to the computation side. Motivated by them, we developed the KSA V2, which not only achieves a more flexible KV cache memory compression but also reduces the computation cost in Full attention layer. Specifically, we found that the summary tokens can serve two roles: the KV memory and sparse indexer.
authors: OneRec Team, Chenglong Chu, Guohong Mu, Guowang Zhang, Hao Peng, Hui Wang, Jian Liang, Jiangxia Cao, Jiao Ou, Jiaxin Deng, Lu Ren, Muhao Wei, Ruiming Tang, Tianle Xu, Wenwu Ou, Xingmei Wang, Zhixin Ling, Zhiyuan Liang, Ziqi Wang, Chaoyi Ma, Haixiao Gao, Kuo Cai, Renpu Liu, Ruochen Yang, Wenlong Xu, Xinqi Jin, Yan Sun, Yifan Wang, Yingzhi He, Yiyu Wang, Yusen Huo, Zhaojie Liu, Zihan Zhou
bullets: Addresses fixed summary-compression windows across layers, which limit flexible KV-cache compression.
Reduces wasted computation in full-attention layers that previously ignored summary tokens while still incurring quadratic prefilling cost.
Uses summary tokens in two roles: compressed KV memory and sparse indexing.
Targets both more flexible KV-cache memory compression and lower full-attention computation cost.
papers.selection_reason: Summary-token attention with flexible KV cache compression and reduced full-attention cost; fits efficient AI and long-context LLM methods.
papers.title: Kwai Summary Attention V2 Technical Report
papers.tldr: KSA V2 makes hybrid summary-token attention more flexible and efficient by separating summary tokens’ KV-memory and sparse-indexing roles.

papers.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) are shaped by the spectral structure induced by their input encodings and activation functions. Existing methods improve fitting primarily by modifying which frequencies are available to the network, through coordinate encodings or periodic nonlinearities. However, frequency access is not the only bottleneck: signals with localized or spatially varying structure require the network to efficiently compose frequencies into multi-harmonic internal responses. We introduce learnable spectral activations (LSA), which replace fixed neuron-level nonlinearities with a residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training. LSA does not expand the asymptotic function class. Instead, it changes the factorization of the representation: linear weights select features while activation coefficients control spectral shaping, and the two are updated by separate gradients. Because the activation output is affine in the coefficients given fixed pre-activations, spectral tuning becomes a more direct subproblem compared to architectures where it is entangled with feature selection. Empirically, this factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in the leading eigenmodes of the neural tangent kernel, consistent with improved optimization behavior. Across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks, LSA also improves reconstruction quality.
bullets: Problem: Existing encodings and periodic activations expand frequency access but may struggle with localized or spatially varying structures requiring multi-harmonic composition.
Method: Replace fixed activations with residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training.
Key idea: Linear weights select features while activation coefficients independently control spectral shaping, without expanding the asymptotic function class.

Result: The factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in leading neural tangent kernel eigenmodes and improves reconstruction quality across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces learnable spectral activations for implicit neural representations, relevant to 3D vision and efficient representation learning.
papers.title: Learnable Spectral Activations
papers.tldr: Learnable Spectral Activations improve implicit neural representations by learning how neurons compose frequencies, enabling better optimization and reconstruction across several signal domains.

papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards improves reasoning, while the allocation of learning signal shapes which solutions remain accessible under repeated sampling. Group-relative objectives assign equal advantages to equally rewarded responses, making aggregate credit proportional to sampled mode frequency. We introduce Exploration-Preserving Policy Optimization (ExPPO), a lightweight advantage-shaping rule that redistributes credit using prompt-relative, length-normalized response surprisal and prompt pass rate. ExPPO combines bounded shaping with shared normalization to preserve verifier polarity and approximately maintain each prompt group's total absolute sequence-advantage mass. Our analysis characterizes response-level credit allocation alongside sampled mode updates, deriving local conditions for gains in entropy and correct-mode discovery. Experiments show improved in-domain and out-of-domain reasoning coverage, higher aggregate response accuracy, and strong coverage at large sampling budgets. A controlled multi-answer evaluation further demonstrates increased correct-mode yield and gains in diversity among verified-correct responses. Code is available at https://github.com/jinhangzhan/ExPPO
bullets: Addresses group-relative objectives that can concentrate learning on frequently sampled solution modes.
Uses prompt-relative, length-normalized response surprisal and prompt pass rate to redistribute credit.
Applies bounded shaping and shared normalization to preserve verifier polarity and approximately conserve each prompt group’s absolute advantage mass.
Analysis links response-level credit allocation to entropy and correct-mode discovery.
Experiments report improved in- and out-of-domain coverage, aggregate accuracy, large-budget coverage, and diversity among verified-correct responses.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a policy optimization method for RL that preserves exploration, relevant to robot learning and efficient credit assignment.
papers.title: Exploration-Preserving Policy Optimization
papers.tldr: ExPPO reshapes reinforcement-learning advantages to preserve exploration while improving correct-solution discovery and reasoning coverage.

papers.abstract: The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank $I + AB^\top$ residual structure. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale ($+$0.05\% to $+$0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by $4\times$ vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and $2\times$ vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, $S{=}4096$). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by $+$0.70\,/\,$+$2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.
authors: Xibo Ding, Guoxia Wang, Jinle Zeng, Jiabin Yang, Sirui Tao, Chao Yang, Dianhai Yu
bullets: Targets the trade-off among KV-cache size, training/prefill compute, and model quality in long-context LLMs.
Uses two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix restores virtual query-head diversity, while Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features with a low-rank residual structure.
The operations can be folded into existing projections at inference, yielding a standard GQA-2 model compatible with GQA optimizations and Tensor Core decoding.
Across four model scales, VHA improves over GQA while reducing KV cache by 2–4× and training/prefill FLOPs by 7.9% in one reported setting.
On industrial MoE evaluations, VHA outperforms MLA and GQA and achieves higher long-context RULER scores than GQA while using fewer KV heads.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a linear attention variant that reduces KV cache size and training/prefill FLOPs for long-context LLMs, directly advancing efficient attention and KV-cache efficiency.
papers.title: Virtual Head Attention
papers.tldr: Virtual Head Attention (VHA) reduces KV-cache and compute costs while maintaining or improving long-context language-model quality over standard attention alternatives.

papers.abstract: Post-hoc linearization is an attractive way to accelerate pretrained Video Diffusion Transformers (Video DiTs), yet existing methods largely treat the quality loss induced by attention replacement as a recovery problem. We show that a more fundamental bottleneck lies upstream: \emph{initialization}. Random initialization discards pretrained knowledge, whereas manual weight reuse transfers it through rigid and incomplete source--target correspondences. We introduce \textbf{LinMorph}, which recasts Video DiT linearization as a learnable softmax-to-linear weight transformation problem. Instead of copying predefined counterparts, LinMorph learns a cross-parameter morphism that lets each target Gated DeltaNet (GDN) parameter draw jointly from pretrained query, key, value, and output projections, including for parameters with no direct softmax counterpart. A single morphism is shared across layers and learned through local teacher alignment, while producing layer-specific initializations from their respective pretrained weights. The resulting weights are then materialized as independent GDN modules for progressive distillation and joint recovery.Since the morphism operates in weight space rather than token space, it can be learned on short, low-resolution clips and directly reused at larger video scales. Across pretrained Video DiTs, LinMorph enables markedly faster recovery and better final generation quality than random initialization and heuristic weight reuse. Results show that efficient linearization depends not only on how a converted model is recovered, but critically on how pretrained knowledge is transferred before recovery. Project page: https://lonelyling.github.io/LinMorph.
authors: Lingyi Long, Congyue Zhao, Xiaoou Li, Yanmin Qian, Tao Huang
bullets: Identifies initialization—not only post-conversion recovery—as a key bottleneck in Video DiT linearization.
Learns a shared cross-parameter softmax-to-linear morphism instead of relying on random initialization or rigid weight copying.
Allows each GDN parameter to combine information from pretrained query, key, value, and output projections, including unmatched parameters.
Uses local teacher alignment on short, low-resolution clips, then applies layer-specific transformed weights for progressive distillation and recovery.
Reports faster recovery and better final generation quality across pretrained Video DiTs than random or heuristic initialization.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a weight-morphing method to linearize Video Diffusion Transformers, improving efficiency of video DiT inference.
papers.title: LinMorph: Learning to Morph Weights for Efficient Video DiT Linearization
papers.tldr: LinMorph learns how to transfer pretrained attention weights into linear Gated DeltaNet modules, enabling faster Video DiT linearization with better recovered quality.

papers.abstract: Long-context training of large language and multimodal models couples structured attention masks (document, prefix-LM, share-question, sliding-window, block-sparse) with multi-node context parallelism, making the mask a dominant bottleneck. FlashMask's column-wise sparse mask compresses them from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n)$ via four query-axis boundary vectors, covering broad structured patterns. Implemented for Ampere GPUs, it neither exploits FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA warp-specialized pipeline on Hopper nor supports distribution. The column-wise sparse mask is indexed by key positions but stores query-axis interval boundaries. Under any multi-chunk context-parallel assignment, it reduces per-rank mask localization to a provably zero-communication \emph{clip--shift--max} on the boundary vectors, compatible with the single-GPU kernel. FlashMask-3 introduces a mask-aware Hopper kernel with three-role warp specialization atop FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA pipeline, plus a mask-aware distributed extension: zero-communication mask localization, a sparsity-aware load balancer (HCC-IPO), and a mask-aware compute-communication overlap with mask-driven communication pruning, whose forward all-gather uses topology-aware hierarchical routing. On a single H100 across 12 masks at 4K--128K context, it improves achieved TFLOPs over FlashMask, FlexAttention, and MagiAttention by 45--141%, 34--71%, and 2--44%. At context-parallel degrees 4--32 with 8K sequence per device, it attains 31--75% compute-communication overlap efficiency and improves throughput over Megatron-Core CP ring, Megatron-Core CP all-gather, and MagiAttention by $1.80\times$--$3.71\times$, $1.71\times$--$2.92\times$, and $1.09\times$--$1.46\times$. In end-to-end training of a 118B-A14B MoE at 128K on 128 H100 GPUs, it raises throughput by 7.3--11.0% over a Dual Chunk all-gather baseline, with attention forward+backward 24.5--44.9% faster.
authors: Guoxia Wang, Qianyue He, Siming Wu, Haoyang Xie, Qiwen Bao, Jinle Zeng, Jiabin Yang, Tian Wu, Dianhai Yu
bullets: Targets the bottleneck of structured attention masks in long-context, multi-node training.
Uses a Hopper-optimized FlashAttention-3 kernel with TMA/WGMMA and three-role warp specialization.
Provides zero-communication mask localization via a clip–shift–max operation, plus load balancing and mask-aware communication overlap with pruning.
On a single H100, improves achieved TFLOPs by 2–141% over prior mask-aware attention systems across 12 masks and 4K–128K contexts.
Across 4–32 context-parallel degrees, improves throughput by up to 3.71×; in 128K end-to-end MoE training, raises throughput by 7.3–11.0%.
papers.selection_reason: Mask-aware distributed attention for long-context LLM training; directly improves attention efficiency and long-context capability.
papers.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention
papers.tldr: FlashMask-3 makes structured, mask-aware attention efficient on Hopper GPUs and across distributed context parallelism, delivering substantial kernel and end-to-end training speedups.

papers.abstract: Diffusion language models apply bidirectional attention over the whole context at every denoising step, so a longer context makes each step substantially more expensive. Sparsifying only at inference leaves the pretrained weights unchanged, so the model is never trained under the sparse pattern it runs with. We propose Prefilling-dLLM v2, which continues training a diffusion language model so that it routes with its native mask token. One mask is appended at the end of each chunk, and a learned role offset marks it as a routing slot. On every fourth layer, a query keeps a bidirectional local window and the top-K chunks scored from that mask; the other layers use a bidirectional sliding window. Starting from Dream-v0-Base-7B extended to 16K with YaRN, we compare Prefilling-dLLM v2 with bidirectional NSA, DSA, and SWA under the same layout, key budget, and dense initialization, using the same Fast-dLLM decoder. With the YaRN factor scaled to the evaluation length, Prefilling-dLLM v2 leads the other sparse methods on all three RULER tasks from 16K to 128K. Its mean accuracy at 128K is 7.4 points above NSA, the next sparse model, while DSA and SWA remain near zero. At the same length, decoding is 172x faster than with full dense attention.
authors: Qi Han, Jing Xiong, Ziyuan Zhang, Ngai Wong
bullets: Addresses the high per-step cost of bidirectional full-context attention in diffusion language models.
Adds one learned routing mask per chunk; every fourth layer selects the top-K chunks while other layers use local sliding-window attention.
Continued training aligns the model with the sparse attention pattern used at inference.
Outperforms bidirectional NSA, DSA, and SWA across three RULER tasks from 16K to 128K; at 128K, it is 7.4 accuracy points above NSA.
Achieves 172× faster decoding than dense attention at 128K, within the evaluated setup and context range.
papers.selection_reason: Learned chunk routing and sparse attention for long-context diffusion language models directly address efficient attention and long-context processing.
papers.title: Prefilling-dLLM v2: Learned Chunk Routing for Long-Context Diffusion Language Models
papers.tldr: Prefilling-dLLM v2 trains a diffusion language model to route attention through learned chunk-level mask tokens, enabling efficient long-context decoding while preserving strong retrieval performance.

papers.abstract: Recent video super-resolution (VSR) models achieve efficient one-step generation through diffusion distillation. However, high-resolution inference remains costly, and distilled models are difficult to align with human preferences. These challenges call for improvements in both model architecture and training strategy. We present \textbf{FlashVSR+} to address both limitations. On the architecture side, we introduce hybrid attention based on the strong locality observed in pretrained VSR models, while retaining sparse global interaction for long-range consistency. It achieves up to $2\times$ DiT speedup and 45\% lower peak memory, enabling spatially untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090. On the training side, we propose Reward-Yield Distribution Matching Distillation (Ry-DMD) for preference-aligned one-step generation. Ry-DMD uses reward-weighted teacher rollouts to incorporate black-box rewards into distribution matching, without backpropagating through the reward model. We further show that Ry-DMD generalizes beyond VSR to T2I generation. Together, FlashVSR+ delivers stronger restoration quality and substantially improves high-resolution efficiency, with consistent gains in user preference. We release our code, models, and training data at \href{https://www.flashvsr.tech}{\textcolor{FlashBlue}{\textbf{www.flashvsr.tech}}}.
authors: Ruchang Yao, Shi Guo, Junhao Zhuang, Mingde Yao, Xin Cai, Jiahao Zhan, Bin Fu, Xinyuan Chen, Yu Qiao, Tianfan Xue
bullets: Targets the high inference cost of high-resolution VSR and the difficulty of aligning distilled models with human preferences.
Uses hybrid attention that emphasizes local interactions while preserving sparse global context for long-range consistency.
Introduces Reward-Yield Distribution Matching Distillation (Ry-DMD), which uses reward-weighted teacher rollouts without backpropagating through the reward model.
Reports up to 2× DiT speedup and 45% lower peak memory, enabling untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090.
Achieves stronger restoration quality and consistent user-preference gains; Ry-DMD also generalizes to text-to-image generation.
papers.selection_reason: Efficient video super-resolution via diffusion distillation and hybrid attention, relevant to video diffusion and efficient attention.
papers.title: FlashVSR+: Efficient Video Super-Resolution via Hybrid Attention and Reward-Yield Distribution Matching
papers.tldr: FlashVSR+ makes one-step video super-resolution faster and more preference-aligned through hybrid attention and reward-weighted distillation.

papers.abstract: Generating images beyond the training resolution of Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) remains challenging, as the number of tokens grows rapidly with resolution, full attention becomes expensive, and outputs often suffer from structural distortions and degraded detail. We identify uniform full attention as the common source of both problems. Attending to all tokens at every step causes quadratic cost and exposes the model to more tokens and relative distances beyond the training range, pushing the model out of distribution. We observe that attention's effective receptive field narrows during denoising, from global in early steps that form structure to local in later steps that refine details. We propose AReA, a training-free attention mechanism whose receptive field evolves from coarse to fine, following the denoising progression. In early steps, AReA applies cross-scale coarse attention over downsampled keys and values, capturing global context, while in later steps it applies local attention within progressively shrinking windows. Without additional parameters or training, experiments show that AReA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art training-free baselines across target resolutions and different models, while also being faster and more efficient.
authors: Javad Rajabi, Koorosh Roohi, David B. Lindell, Babak Taati
bullets: Addresses quadratic full-attention costs and structural/detail degradation when DiTs generate beyond training resolution.
Uses coarse cross-scale attention in early denoising steps to capture global structure.
Progressively switches to shrinking-window local attention in later steps for detail refinement.
Training-free and adds no parameters, while reported experiments show consistent gains over training-free baselines with improved speed and efficiency.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces AReA, a training-free attention mechanism that adapts receptive fields from coarse to fine, directly improving efficiency in high-resolution Diffusion Transformers.
papers.title: AReA: Adaptive Receptive-Field Attention for Efficient High-Resolution Diffusion Transformers
papers.tldr: AReA enables more efficient high-resolution Diffusion Transformers by adapting attention from global to local as denoising progresses.

papers.abstract: Linear-time sequence models typically store long-context information in a recurrent state. A fixed-size state limits how much information can be stored, while hybrid architectures that add full attention for better recall incur quadratic sequence cost. Alternatively, sparse attention with continued pretraining (CPT) can extend the effective context length. Generalization beyond the trained length remains challenging, however, and CPT can be costly. We introduce FreeSolo, a native sparse attention mechanism with a short-range sliding window branch and a long-range branch that selects keypoint cells for direct token attention. Its linear-time variant, FS-L, learns to prune the prefix before query-dependent selection through short CPT. FS-B searches balanced trees with $O(N\log^2 N)$ algorithmic cost including radix-sort construction. FreeSolo demonstrates better zero-shot length extrapolation than the baselines without long-context fine-tuning.
authors: Zekun Shi, Alastair James Arthur Price
bullets: Addresses the limited memory of fixed-size recurrent states and the quadratic cost of full attention.
Combines a short-range sliding-window branch with a long-range branch that selects keypoint cells for direct token attention.
FS-L prunes the prefix before query-dependent selection, while FS-B searches balanced trees with O(N log² N) cost.
The method shows better zero-shot length extrapolation than baselines without long-context fine-tuning.
papers.selection_reason: Linear-time sparse attention with zero-shot length extrapolation, relevant to efficient attention and long-context processing.
papers.title: FreeSolo: Linear-time Sparse Attention with Zero-Shot Length Extrapolation
papers.tldr: FreeSolo is a sparse-attention mechanism that enables linear-time long-context modeling and stronger zero-shot length extrapolation without long-context fine-tuning.

papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics jointly captures molecular state, tissue morphology, and spatial organization, yet spatial-domain methods are typically compared only at late training checkpoints, obscuring differences in convergence efficiency. We introduce MP-MNCA, a morphology-prior masked neighbor cross-attention framework that preserves the full 3,000 dimensional highly-variable-gene representation while selectively routing molecular information across spatial neighbors, with histological similarity incorporated as a continuous attention prior under a self-supervised masked neighbor-contrastive objective. Across 12 heterogeneous human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) sections, MP-MNCA is evaluated against established spatial-domain baselines using both convergence trajectories and epoch-wise spatial-domain visualizations. Our results show that MP-MNCA (i) reaches coherent spatial-domain structure in substantially fewer training epochs, as reflected quantitatively by convergence curves and qualitatively by progressive spatial grids, and (ii) maintains strong clustering quality, achieving a mean peak refined ARI of 0.546 versus 0.549 for the strongest baseline (STAIG), while attaining the highest mean refined NMI of 0.657 versus 0.640. Moreover, MP-MNCA outperforms STAIG on 7 of 12 sections in ARI and 11 of 12 in NMI, demonstrating faster convergence without sacrificing spatial-domain quality.
bullets: Addresses the limited comparison of spatial-domain methods during training by evaluating convergence trajectories and epoch-wise spatial visualizations.
Preserves the full 3,000-dimensional highly variable gene representation and selectively routes molecular information across spatial neighbors.
Uses histological similarity as a continuous attention prior within a self-supervised masked neighbor-contrastive objective.
Across 12 human DLPFC sections, it reaches coherent spatial structure in fewer epochs than established baselines.
Its mean peak refined ARI is 0.546 versus 0.549 for STAIG, while mean refined NMI is higher at 0.657 versus 0.640; it outperforms STAIG on 7/12 sections in ARI and 11/12 in NMI.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a novel attention mechanism (Masked Neighbor Cross-Attention) designed for efficiency in spatial domain identification. The technical contribution of an efficient attention mechanism is transferable to the Efficient AI topic.
papers.title: MP-MNCA: Morphology-Prior Masked Neighbor Cross-Attention for Efficient Spatial Domain Identification
papers.tldr: MP-MNCA accelerates spatial-domain identification in spatial transcriptomics by combining morphology-guided neighbor attention with masked contrastive learning, while preserving competitive clustering quality.

papers.abstract: Spiking Transformers achieve energy efficiency by discarding softmax normalization in favor of thresholded, binary attention. However, this removal breaks the thermodynamic framework used to analyze attention networks, as the normalized measure and partition function cease to exist. We restore this theoretical foundation by proving that softmax-free spiking attention operates exactly as the zero-temperature limit of a product of independent two-level systems. This correspondence places spiking attention strictly in the frozen ordered phase of the thermodynamic phase diagram for all inputs. Consequently, the entropic cost of organizing attention collapses, replaced by a Landauer-type physical floor governed by action-potential generation. Furthermore, this ordered-phase pinning mathematically explains the optimization difficulty caused by vanishing surrogate gradients. We validate this theory with forward-relaxation experiments, placing both standard and neuromorphic attention mechanisms on a unified thermodynamic axis.
authors: Roberto C. Sotero, Pouya Taghipour, Jose M. Sanchez-Bornot
bullets: Reintroduces a thermodynamic framework for binary, thresholded attention without softmax normalization.
